**Breaking post output: the posted Z of each existing part-off moves by half a blade width toward the bar.** For example: end face Z-70, 3 mm blade, orientation 2: the old program has `G01 X0 Z-71.5`, the new program has `G01 X0. Z-73.`.

## After the third read (head 6b845e5ef)

- **A. The free end is read on the part's own axis.** The door of 6c18258d1 tested document +Z. A model drawn lying down (along X) is stood up with TURN, so document Z is horizontal in OP10 and in an OP20 flip alike, and the flip passed. Now:
  - The kept side matters only when the model goes on past the plane on both sides (`parting_law::plane_inside_model`). At an end of the model, the model is the part, so any setup generates.
  - There, the Part arm refuses with `setup_align::part_off_problem`. It fits the part's own turning axis on the setup-frame facets (`multiaxis::axis::fit`) and reads it back into the document frame.
  - The sign: the as-modelled setup (no alignment) holds document +Z up the spindle.
  - A part modelled standing must point its document-up end up the spindle by 0.5 or more. At -0.5 or less it is "end for end". Between the two it is "no clear hold". There is no decision at 0.
  - A part modelled lying down has no as-modelled hold, so the setup cannot say which end is free: refused.
- **B. Saved projects.** The Part stamp has the salt `part-off-kerf-side-v1`, so a part-off saved before this PR loads Stale. The post refuses it until it is generated again. The other blade kinds keep their stamps.
- **Behaviour that worked on main and is refused now.** A part-off with the plane inside the model is refused in these setups:
  - an aligned setup that does not hold the part as modelled (for example the OP20 flip);
  - a setup with a part that is modelled lying down. `setup_align_lathe.rs` loses its PT1 for this reason.

  #3469 (a parameter for the side to keep) is the way back.

| case | main | 6c18258d1 | 6b845e5ef |
|---|---|---|---|
| X-drawn pin under TURN, plane at its end | Z-71.5 | Z-73 | Z-73 |
| X-drawn stubbed pin, plane inside, under TURN and TURN [-90,0,90] | generates | **generates, no refusal** | refused by name |
| Z-drawn stubbed pin, spin [0,0,90] about the spindle | Z-71.5 | Z-73 | Z-73 |
| saved part-off (fixture recorded on main), after load | Ok, posts Z-71.5 | **Ok, posts Z-71.5** | Stale, the post is refused; generated again it posts Z-73 |

## After the two re-reads (heads 9dadc2efd and 6c18258d1)

1. First re-read (blocker): a plane inside the model took its scrap side from the stock overhang. A model with its grip stub (Z-84..0, plane Z-70) under a stock with a 0.1 mm front facing allowance parted Z-70..-67, 3 mm into the part. Fix: the scrap side is the chuck side (`parting_law::chuck_side`), never a guess from the stock. No setup or machine field names the spindle that holds the bar, so the chuck is at lower Z (ISO 841). A plane with the whole model on the chuck side is refused by name. `part_kerf_refusal` reads the side by itself, not from the kernel.
2. Second re-read (blocker): the setup alignment is baked into the facets. In an OP20 flip setup the chuck holds the finished part, and the free end is scrap. Fix: `collect_job` refuses a Part op when `setup_align::reverses_axis` holds. The predicate is: the alignment turns document +Z to a negative setup Z. It covers each reversal of the turning axis, not only the flip preset. Refusal text: "a part-off cannot run in this setup: the setup holds the part end for end, so the chuck holds the finished part and the free end is the piece the blade would cut off as the part. The side to keep cannot be chosen yet - part off in a setup that holds the bar as modelled, or face the free end to length instead".
3. The note `CHUCK_NOTE` is now in plain words. It goes on the path only where the rule decides what is kept, that is, when the model is on both sides of the plane.

Hand trace (plane Z-70, 3 mm blade, orientation 2): path centre Z-71.5, posted Z-73, blade span Z-73..-70.

Red, then green readings:

| case | 6a82e57e9 | 9dadc2efd | 6c18258d1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| (c) issue case, plane at the model end | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 |
| (a) stub model, stock flush at the front | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 |
| (b) stub model, 0.1 / 1 / 5 mm front allowance | **Z-70..-67** | Z-73..-70 | Z-73..-70 |
| flip setup, stub model, plane Z-14 | - | **generates, no refusal** | refused by name |

The readings of 6a82e57e9 come from a scratch test on the API of that head. The test was not committed.

## Cause

The Part operation used its parting plane (Bottom Z) as the centre line of the blade. The kernel set the CL at `station_of(parting_z)` and the band at ± w/2 (`crates/motion/src/turning/parting.rs`, old lines 66-69). The #641 shift then posts the corner of the blade. For the end face Z-70 of #3452, the kerf was Z-71.5..-68.5. It removed 1.5 mm and the back chamfer of the finished part. Nothing caught it:

- The refusal "nothing to part" compared the kerf with the model silhouette only. Thus it refused the correct kerf beside the part end.
- The revolved-blade scan reads a through-axis kerf as scrap by design. Thus it was silent.
- `verify` does not judge turning.

## What changed

- **The kerf side** (`crates/motion/src/turning/parting_law.rs`, new). The plane is the end face of the finished part. The whole kerf is on the chuck side (lower Z), and one flank is on the plane. The CL is half a blade from the plane. A plane with the whole model on the chuck side is refused: `nothing to part - the model (Z0.000 to Z70.000) stands wholly on the chuck side (lower Z) of the parting plane Z70.000; the part is what stands above the plane, away from the chuck`. A part held from +Z (a sub-spindle, a mirrored setup) cannot be stated yet: #3469.
- **The flipped setup** (`crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`, `crates/app/src/setup_align.rs`): see "After the two re-reads", point 2.
- **The refusal** (`parting.rs`). It compares the kerf with the bar: the model span plus the two ends of the stock. It accepts the correct kerf past the end of the part when the bar continues. If the kerf does not touch the bar, it refuses and gives the values. Example: `nothing to part - the 3.000 mm kerf beside the parting plane (Z-73.000 to Z-70.000) does not meet the bar (Z-70.000 to Z0.000); set the setup's stock if the bar runs on past the part`. `StockEnv` gets `s_bot` (the near end of the bar), and `turning_stock::read` fills it.
- **The generation verdict** (`part_kerf_refusal`, called in the Part arm of `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`). A part-off path is refused (`GenError`, so it is never posted) if a cutting move puts the band of the blade into material of the finished part by more than 1 µm. The band is the width of the blade, never wider. Example: `the part-off cuts into the finished part: move 0 puts the 3.000 mm blade at Z-71.500 to Z-68.500, 1.500 mm past the part's end face at Z-70.000 - the whole kerf must stand on the chuck side (lower Z) of that face`. It reads the side from the chuck alone, so a kerf put on the wrong side for any reason is caught. It cannot prove the intent of the user when the model is on both sides of the plane. There the path says which rule it used (`CHUCK_NOTE`).
- **The other blade kinds.** Groove Rough and Groove Finish do not have this fault. Their kerf stays inside the groove window by construction: `crates/motion/src/turning/blade.rs:170-171` `let lo_c = if s_lo <= d_lo { s_lo } else { s_lo + half }; let hi_c = if s_hi >= d_hi { s_hi } else { s_hi - half };`. The new law runs only for Part, so it cannot refuse a legal groove. Relief and face groove are not separate kinds (`params.rs`). Threading and Form Turning are not blade cuts (`posting_nose::is_blade_cut`). Their goldens do not change.
- The decision record: `docs/decisions/3452-part-off-kerf-side.md`.

## The case of the issue, posted (orientation 2, 3 mm blade, end face Z-70)

| before (main) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|
| CL Z-70, kerf Z-71.5..-68.5 | CL Z-71.5, kerf Z-73..-70 |
| `G01 X30 Z-71.5` ... `G01 X0 Z-71.5` | `G01 X30 Z-73.` ... `G01 X0. Z-73.` |
| part 68.5 mm, chamfer removed | part 70 mm, chamfer kept |

With orientation 1 (+Z corner) the same kerf posts Z-70 (on the face). On main it posted Z-68.5, which is the RED output of `the_plus_z_corner_posts_the_end_face_itself`.

Golden `groove_part.nc` (fanuc-lathe, plane Z-10, 3 mm blade, orientation 2):

```
before                       after
(PART LOAD ADVANCE 30)       (PART LOAD ADVANCE 30)
G00 X12.1 Z-11.5             G00 X12.1 Z-13.
G01 X11. Z-11.5 F0.03        G01 X11. Z-13. F0.03
...                          ...
G01 X0. Z-11.5 F0.03         G01 X0. Z-13. F0.03
```

## Tests (red on main, then green)

- `crates/app/tests/lathe_part_off_kerf.rs` (new; it uses only the API of main, and was run on main with the fix stashed):
  - `a_part_off_at_the_end_face_keeps_the_whole_part`: RED on main `the kerf Z-71.5..Z-68.5 enters the part past its end face Z-70`. GREEN: each posted feed is at Z-73, and the part is 70 mm long.
  - `the_plus_z_corner_posts_the_end_face_itself`: RED on main `the +Z corner posts Z-70: [-68.5, ...]`. GREEN.
  - `a_flipped_setup_refuses_the_part_off_by_name`: RED on 9dadc2efd (`the part-off is refused: ()`). GREEN: the stubbed model in the flip setup is refused by name. The flipped part-only pin, parted at its +Z end, is refused by `no_part_past_plane`.
  - `a_setup_as_modelled_parts_the_stubbed_pin_behind_the_end_face`: the stubbed pin, plane Z-70 inside the model, posts Z-73, as modelled and with a spin about the spindle.
  - `a_part_modelled_lying_down_parts_only_at_its_end`: RED on 6c18258d1 (the lying stub generated). GREEN: the lying pin under TURN posts Z-73. The lying stub is refused under TURN and under TURN [-90,0,90].
- `crates/app/tests/part_off_saved_before_3452.rs` (new) with `crates/app/tests/fixtures/part_off_pre_3452.camproj`. The fixture was recorded on main 6679b1b4b by the env-gated `record_the_pre_3452_fixture`. `a_part_off_saved_before_3452_loads_stale_and_does_not_post` is RED on main and on 6c18258d1 (`left: Ok, right: Stale`). GREEN: the fixture holds the old CL Z-70. After load P1 is Stale and G1 (a groove finish) is Ok. The post is refused with `P1: inputs moved since generation`. Generated again, P1 has CL Z-71.5 and posts.
- `crates/motion/tests/turning_part_kerf.rs` (new; it uses the new API, so on main it does not compile):
  - `the_issue_case_kerf_stands_behind_the_end_face`: Ø30 pin Z-70..0 with a 1 x 45° back chamfer, 3 mm blade, bar to Z-84. Each blade band is within Z-73..-70 ± 1 µm. The part keeps 70 mm. The verdict and the meridian scan are silent. No note (the plane is at the end of the model).
  - `a_front_facing_allowance_never_turns_the_kerf_into_the_part`: the stubbed model with front allowances 0, 0.1, 1 and 5 mm. The kerf is always Z-73..-70, and the path has the note.
  - `a_model_wholly_on_the_chuck_side_is_refused_by_name`: the mirrored pin Z0..70 with the plane at Z70 is refused by the kernel and by the verdict.
  - `a_plane_the_model_runs_past_parts_toward_the_chuck`: model Z-40..0, plane Z-20, no stock. The kerf is Z-23..-20.
  - `a_kerf_that_meets_no_bar_is_refused_by_its_numbers`: refused with no stock and with a bar that ends at the face, accepted when the bar continues. The message gives the kerf and bar spans.
  - `the_verdict_refuses_a_kerf_into_the_part`: a hand-built plunge centred on the plane (the old output) is refused and the message gives 1.500 mm. 2 µm into the part is refused. A kerf put wholly on the part side (CL Z-68.5 on the stubbed model) is refused with "Z-70.000 to Z-67.000" and "3.000 mm past". A blade on the face or past it passes. A width of 0 or an empty model is refused (a judge that cannot measure never reports silence).

## Changed pins and goldens (old value -> new value, why)

All changes have the same cause: the CL moves from the plane to plane - w/2 (the waste side).

- `crates/app/tests/lathe_blade_corner.rs` `a_part_off_leaves_the_part_the_verified_kerf_leaves`: plane Z-20, 3 mm. Posted plunges for corners None/2, 1, 6: -21.5/-18.5/-20 -> -23/-20/-21.5. The back face of the part: -18.5 -> -20.
- `crates/app/tests/lathe_post.rs` `groove_and_part_post_to_the_lathe_golden`: `Z-11.5` -> `Z-13.`.
- `crates/app/tests/catalog_groove_part_off.rs`: `G01 X0 Z13.5` -> `Z12`. A new assertion is added: no part-off feed puts the blade above the end face Z15.
- `crates/app/tests/turning_blade.rs` `a_part_op_severs_the_bar_in_the_document`: CL z -10 -> -11.5.
- `crates/motion/tests/turning_blade.rs`:
  - `parting_ladders_to_the_axis_in_one_center`: centre station 0 -> -1 (2 mm blade).
  - `every_refusal_names_itself`: the plane z 50 is above the wall (top z 40). The text "off the end of the bar" -> "stands wholly on the chuck side", which is the refusal that now comes first.
- `crates/motion/tests/turning_stock.rs`, `turning_contour_stock.rs`: `StockEnv` literals get `s_bot: f64::NAN` (unknown, the same meaning as a non-finite `s_top`).
- Goldens:
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`: 25 part-off lines Z-11.5 -> Z-13. Written with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` by its own test.
  - `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`: 25 lines Z-0.4528 -> Z-0.5118. Written by `lathe_post_inch`.
  - No other line changes.
- Catalog, regenerated by `cargo xtask catalog --case turning/groove-part-off` and `--case turning/cone-thread` (not edited by hand):
  - `groove-part-off.nc` and `cone-thread.nc`: part-off Z13.5 -> Z12. The X ladder is the same, X29 to X0 in 1 mm steps. The old program had one duplicate `G01 X0. Z13.5` (a float rung just above the axis). The new program does not have it.
  - At 6b845e5ef each `.camproj` changes in one more line: the stamp of the Part op (the salt). The stamps of the groove ops do not change.
  - The `.camproj` files are the tool's own rewrite, and the tool always writes the whole file. The catalog files were last written at project format 73, and main writes format 76. The rewrite gives new stamps and new cached paths for all operations. The posted `.nc` of each other operation is byte for byte the same; `example_catalog` regenerates and compares it. Thus the cache differences come from main changes after the last regeneration, not from this PR. The tool has no option to keep the diff smaller. The two review-fix commits change these files by 0 lines in total: the note line was added and then removed.
  - READMEs and the `build.camscript` comment now say the new Z values.

## Gate

The quick gate plan (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`) has 717 steps, more than 80. Thus each touched binary was run alone (debug, `-j 6`), on the final head 6b845e5ef:

- motion: `--lib` 536 passed (10 ignored); `turning_part_kerf` 6; `turning_blade` 11; `turning_stock` 5; `turning_contour_stock` 4. All green.
- app: `lathe_part_off_kerf` 5; `part_off_saved_before_3452` 2; `lathe_blade_corner` 4; `catalog_groove_part_off` 1; `lathe_post` 7; `lathe_post_inch` 6; `turning_blade` 14; `setup_align_lathe` 4; `turning_stock_approach` 3; `drill_prior` 12; `coarse_laws` 6; `project_roundtrip` 76; `--lib -- part stamp` 31; `example_catalog` (filtered: groove-part-off and cone-thread regenerates and rebuilds, plus 2 contract tests) 6. All green.
- clippy `-D warnings`: `-p camcraft-motion --lib --tests` clean. `-p camcraft-app --lib` with the 8 touched test targets clean.

**Heavy lanes** (`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6 cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main`, on the final head 6b845e5ef, release, `--ignored`): `wall 77.5 min, 244 step(s), 0 failed`.

- 1 heavy build (release `--no-run`), 37 motion heavy steps, 206 app heavy steps. All ok.
- The reached turning, lathe and setup lanes are all ok. They include:
  - `turning`, `turning_blade`, `turning_profile`, `turning_contour`, `turning_form`, `turning_bore`, `turning_bore_feeds`, `turning_thread`, `turning_thread_infeed`, `turning_holder`, `turning_holder_steel`, `turning_stock_approach`, `turning_axial_rapids`, `turning_insert_zone`, `turning_hidden_floor`;
  - `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_inch`, `lathe_post_tormach` (with its g30, g76_ladder, g76_start and thread lanes), `lathe_post_g76` (and schedule, sources), `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_thread_dips`, `lathe_post_turn_radius`, `lathe_chuck`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `lathe_field_sim`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `lathe_workholding_kinds`, `lathe_workholding_live`, `sim_lathe_body`;
  - `setup_align_lathe`, `setup_align_mill_turn`, `setup_align_non_mill`, `example_catalog`, `project_roundtrip`.
- Known-fail steps, red as expected (not related to this PR):
  - motion #1950 `the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`;
  - motion #1950 `the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`;
  - app #1950 `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`;
  - app #2849 `fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`.

## Not exercised

- A real control or machine.
- Lathe posts other than `fanuc-lathe.cps` (mm and inch). The posting shim is the same for all of them, but these posts were not run: Tormach PathPilot Lathe (the post of the issue), LinuxCNC lathe, Haas lathe, Sinumerik lathe, and the mill-turn posts.
- The q03 project file of the issue (a QA artifact). Its geometry is rebuilt in the tests from the numbers in the issue.
- The UI (no application window was started).

`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` was already above the 400-line limit (about 4280 lines). This PR adds only 11 lines to its Part arm.

Follow-up (a parameter for the kerf position, default = this behaviour): #3469.

Effort: high (not escalated).

Changelog: Part (part-off) now puts the whole blade kerf on the bar side of the parting plane, which is the end face of the finished part. Before, the kerf was centred on the plane and cut half a blade width into the part (#3452). **Breaking:** the posted Z of existing part-off operations moves by half a blade width toward the bar. Example: end face Z-70, 3 mm blade, orientation 2: Z-71.5 becomes Z-73. A part-off whose kerf does not touch a known bar is refused and the message gives the values. A part-off path that cuts into the finished part is refused at generation. A part-off with the parting plane inside the model is refused in a setup that holds the part end for end, or when the part is modelled lying down, because the side to keep cannot be chosen yet. A part-off saved before this change must be generated again before it posts.

Fixes #3452

title: fix(post): never write an arc block whose written ends coincide
body:
## Cause

Two places turned a short arc into a full circle.

1. The posts. The arc path of each post wrote the end point of an arc record through its own word format (Fanuc inch: four decimals, a 2.54 um step). No post compared the written end with the written start. A short arc under the output step got the same X and Y words as its start and a nonzero I/J. A control reads that block as a full circle. The reporter (thank you, @qsmits, for the clear reproduction `tiny.cnc`) found it with two 1 um arcs (sweep about 0.007 degrees) on the Fanuc inch post. Metric also collides: two ends less than 1 um apart write the same three-decimal word.
2. The stream writer (found by the re-read). The app posts through `cnc::serialize`, which writes each position as whole micrometres. A generator arc with a chord under 1 um (#3463: a fillet can reach 0.09 um) rounded to a record whose end equals its start. The stream reader takes that form as a full turn (`full_circle_raw`), so every post wrote a full circle. Before this PR, the new app test posted `G02 X10.346 Y-2.98 Z2.5 I0. J-50. F800` for a 0.09 um fillet: a full circle of R50 through the part.

## The law

No post writes an arc block whose end point, as written (output unit, precision, work origin and modal words applied), equals its start point in the arc plane, unless the record is a full turn that the dialect writes as one block. The comparison uses the text of the words, not the stream's millimetres. The stream writer never writes a short arc in the stream's full-turn form.

## The change

- The posts: one rule in one place, `arcFate(word)` / `arcFateOf(shape, word)` in the PRELUDE (`crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs`, appended by `Script::load`). Each script calls it with its own word function.
  - `"arc"`: the written in-plane ends differ, or the record turns more than half a circle (its sweep from its direction and centre), or its ends are equal in the stream (the stated full turn), or it states no finite centre (the script's own refusal by name runs). The arc posts as before. No distance band: a true short arc with a tiny chord is still short.
  - `"linear"`: a short arc whose ends coincide as written, while Z (a helix) or a rotary still moves. The post writes its own straight feed move (`onLinear`) to the end point.
  - `"none"`: a short arc whose ends coincide, and nothing changes as written. No motion block. The feed and the modal state are not touched.
- The stream writer: `crates/post/src/post/cnc_arc_lattice.rs`, called by `cnc::serialize` (the one place that the whole-job, per-operation and per-mount paths use: `posting.rs`, `posting_per_op.rs`, `posting_mounts.rs`). The writer tracks the true start of each arc. An arc whose in-plane ends round to the same micrometre and whose true sweep is half a turn or less is written as a `Feed` to its rounded end. A near-full turn and a stated full turn keep their arc record. The record stays, also when nothing moves (a zero-length `Feed`), because the viewer map counts stream records as toolpath moves.
- The stream reader is not made stricter: equal ends stay the stated full-turn form (`full_circle_raw`, with a golden on every post). With the writer fixed, our own streams never use that form for a short arc. The decision file says why a refusal and a zero-sweep reading were dropped.
- The R-word mode (`useRadiusArcs`) comes after the guard. A short arc that the output can show keeps its minor (positive R) solution.
- Klartext no longer refuses the short case. Its refusal stays only for a near-full turn with coincident written ends.
- `heidenhain.cps` `verticalArc`: a record with equal ends in G18/G19 is a full circle of chords. Before, it was one zero-length chord.
- No input refusal: an arc of 0.007 degrees stays legal input.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3442-coincident-arc-blocks.md` (chosen, why, dropped).

## The reporter's file, Fanuc, `--units inch`

Before (each block is a full circle on the control):

```
G03 X0.7135 Y0.2139 Z0.2165 I-0.315 J0. F7.09
G03 X0.7135 Y0.2139 Z0.2165 I-0.315 J0. F7.09
```

After: no arc block. The plunge ends at `X0.7135 Y0.2139`, and the next motion block is the rapid retract. The two arcs move the tool less than 0.0001 in, so the tool is never further from the programmed path than the output step.

## Every shipped post

| Post | Guard site | Guarded | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| carvera | `onCircular` (mm only) | yes | table (b) |
| doosan-dnm | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b), R mode, rotary |
| fanuc | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | (a), (b), (c), R mode, rotary, app tests |
| fanuc-lathe | `meridianArc`, on its X (diameter) and Z words | yes | table (b), lathe witness |
| grbl | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| grblhal | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| haas | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| heidenhain (DIN/ISO) | `onCircular`, after the cycle refusal (mm only) | yes | table (b) |
| heidenhain-klartext | `onCircular`, on its rounded preset values (mm only) | yes | table (b), near-full refusal |
| linuxcnc | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| mach4 | `onCircular`, on the machine-frame words after the trunnion transform | yes | table (b) |
| mazak | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| sinker-iso | refuses every arc (no change) | yes | table (b): no arc block |
| sinumerik | `onCircular`, after `compRefuse` | yes | table (b) |
| sodick-wire | `onCircular`, after `cutOk` | yes | table (b), flat witness |
| tinyg | `onCircular` (its by-name refusal of the short case is replaced) | yes | table (b), app `tinyg_post` |
| tormach | `onCircular` | yes | table (b), R mode |
| tormach-lathe | `meridianArc` | yes | table (b), lathe witness |
| tormach-plasma | `onCircular`, after the compensation refusal | yes | table (b), flat witness |

title: feat(xtask): gate heavy --covers for one heavy run per merge wave
body:
## What changed

- `xtask/src/heavy_covers.rs` (new): `gate heavy --covers <PR>:<head sha>`. The tool refuses a sha that is not a commit, a head that is not an ancestor of `HEAD`, and a working tree with changes. It prints `covers: #<PR> <sha>` for each head and `tree: <HEAD^{tree}>` in the plan header and under the summary. A real run writes `covers.txt` to the gate log directory: the header, each step with its result and note, the counts, the wall time and the verdict. `--dry-run` prints the header and runs nothing.
- `xtask/src/gate_args.rs` (new): `GateArgs` and `parse_gate`, moved from `main.rs` with the new repeatable `--covers` flag. The flag applies to the heavy tier only. A bad value, a repeated PR or another tier is a refusal with the usage text. `main.rs` goes from 407 to 344 lines.
- `xtask/src/main.rs`: the module list, the usage line and the `heavy` arm of `gate()`. With no `--covers`, the behaviour does not change.
- `xtask/src/heavy_covers_tests.rs` (new): 4 tests.
- `AGENTS.md` "Heavy lanes at review": the PR form and the wave form (#3460). "Not run" is never a pass, a PR that merges alone keeps the PR form, and the cut tier stays the final check. A wave record covers a PR only for the head that it names. A safety-floor PR is covered only if the trial tree contains its final head.
- `.claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md`: new step 4a. It makes the trial tree (a detached worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`, `git merge --no-ff` of each PR head in the planner's order onto `origin/main`, never pushed, removed after the run). It runs the gate one time, gives the one fixed comment form (`<!-- heavy-wave: <tree hash> -->`), and says what to do on a red step and when a head is no longer covered.
- `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`: the table row and the wave form bullets.
- `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md`: new section 2e, the two sources of heavy evidence.
- `.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md` step 5: a reviewer accepts a wave record only if its `covers:` line names the current head of the PR, all reached lanes are in it, and its verdict is `PASS`. The reviewer duty of #2568 stays (pinned by `runner_review_requires_heavy_lanes_without_author_results`).
- `docs/decisions/3460-heavy-run-per-wave.md`: chosen, why, dropped, with the maintainer's words.

## The maintainer's words (#3460, 2026-11-22)

> A wave of PRs that the planner groups together gets ONE heavy run on a trial tree of the wave (current `main` plus each PR of the wave). The result is recorded on each PR of the wave (tree hash, lanes, counts). A red step is attributed to a PR, that PR leaves the wave, and the run starts again for the rest.
>
> Rules that stay:
> - "Not run" is never a pass.
> - A PR that merges alone keeps the rule of today.
> - The release tier at the cut stays the final check.

> Safety-floor PRs: the wave run covers them only if the trial tree contains their final head.

## Dry run of the flag on this head (fe265cdc2)

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --covers 3460:fe265cdc2a13c015c4db22b32080138fd25163d4 --covers 3467:fe265cdc2a13c015c4db22b32080138fd25163d4 --dry-run`

```
covers: #3460 fe265cdc2a13c015c4db22b32080138fd25163d4
covers: #3467 fe265cdc2a13c015c4db22b32080138fd25163d4
tree: ad917da9b71262dd58c35ad5032aba1c4a299267
base: origin/main 5326584a7abae6ebc35228ad1e871e293c1103c3
changed since origin/main: 11 file(s)
heavy plan (release --ignored lanes the diff reaches, #2568):
  the diff reaches no heavy lane: nothing to run
...
== gate summary (heavy) - logs in ...\gate-logs\heavy-20261122-151711
  wall 0.0 min, 0 step(s), 0 failed
  covers: #3460 fe265cdc2a13c015c4db22b32080138fd25163d4
  covers: #3467 fe265cdc2a13c015c4db22b32080138fd25163d4
  tree: ad917da9b71262dd58c35ad5032aba1c4a299267
  base: origin/main 5326584a7abae6ebc35228ad1e871e293c1103c3
  planned: 0 step(s), dry run: nothing ran
  the wave reaches no heavy lane
```

## Changes after the review (comment 7081027933) and the decision on #3467

- Blocker 1: `--covers` refuses `--only` and `--failed` with the usage text (`gate_args.rs`). The record has `counts: <planned> planned, <ran> ran, <ok> ok, <failed> failed`. The verdict is `INCOMPLETE` when a planned step did not run (`heavy_covers::verdict`). Only `PASS` covers a head.
- Blocker 2: `merge-ready` step 4a item 10: a `SAME` or `MECHANICAL` refresh keeps the heavy result of a wave-2 PR. A `DELTA` or `NEW CODE` refresh needs a new result (its own run, or a wave record that names the new head). AGENTS.md says the same in the PR form.
- Note 1: `<!-- heavy-wave: ... -->` is in the AGENTS.md list of fixed strings and in the collaborator-marker rule.
- Note 2: the header, the summary and `covers.txt` print `base: <ref> <merge-base sha>`. Step 4a item 9: if `origin/main` moved after the run, run the planner again. A PR whose trial merge is no longer clean leaves the wave.
- Note 3: a plan with no step gives `verdict: NO LANE` and the line "the wave reaches no heavy lane", in the tool and in the comment form.
- #3467 (maintainer decision, 2026-11-22): new stable rule **Owed heavy result** in AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review". A review of a `P3` or lower PR can set `merge-ready` with "not run - owed to the wave run before merge" and the owed lanes. The merge waits for a green record that names the final head. A `P1` or `P2` PR (or a PR with no priority label) keeps the strict rule. Text in PR-reviewer step 5 and its review comment line, the `review-prs` skill (2e), the `merge-ready` skill (4a item 11), the `gate` skill and the decision file (second entry, with his words).

> Maintainer decision, 2026-11-22, given in the question dialog: **allowed for P3 and lower only.**
> - A review of a P3 or lower PR may set `merge-ready` while the heavy result says "not run - owed to the wave run before merge". The comment names the owed lanes.
> - The merge (not the review) waits for a green run that covers the final head, with the `--covers <PR>:<sha>` record of #3460.
> - A P1 or P2 PR keeps the strict rule: the heavy result on the head comes before the label `merge-ready`.
> - The coordinator refuses to merge a PR with an owed heavy result until the covering record names the head.

## Tests (head fe265cdc2)

- `cargo test -p xtask -j 6`: `test result: ok. 281 passed; 0 failed` (bin), and all other xtask targets ok.
- Pinning tests:
  - `heavy_covers_tests::covers_is_repeatable_on_the_heavy_tier`
  - `heavy_covers_tests::covers_refuses_other_tiers_and_bad_values` (now also `--covers` with `--only` and `--failed`)
  - `heavy_covers_tests::header_and_record_name_each_head_the_tree_and_the_counts` (now with the `base:` line and the planned count)
  - `heavy_covers_tests::not_run_is_never_a_pass_in_the_record` (new: `INCOMPLETE`, `NO LANE`)
  - `heavy_covers_tests::a_head_that_the_trial_tree_lacks_is_refused` (now also the merge-base sha)
  - `heavy_plan_tests::an_owed_heavy_result_is_allowed_for_p3_and_lower_only` (new, #3467: P3 and lower can defer with the fixed text; P1 and P2 cannot)
  - `heavy_plan_tests::runner_review_requires_heavy_lanes_without_author_results` (unchanged, passes)
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -j 6 -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes: the diff reaches no heavy lane (dry run above).

## Not exercised

- A real wave run: no heavy lane ran, and no `covers.txt` was written by a real run (the text is pinned by the unit test).
- The merge-ready step 4a procedure end to end, and the `heavy-wave` comment on real PRs.

Effort: medium

Process change: yes

Changelog: none

Fixes #3460

title: feat(post): Fanuc rigid tap option writes M29 S before G84
body:
## What changed

- The Fanuc post has a new option, `rigidTapM29` ("Rigid tap M29 before G84"). It is off by default.
- When the option is on, the post writes `M29 S<rpm>` on the block right before each G84 block that opens a cycle group.
- G80 ends rigid mode on the control. Thus each G84 group writes its own M29.
- When the option is on and the section has no spindle speed (for example a touch probe section at 0 rpm), the post refuses the G84 by name. It does not write `M29 S0`.
- This is the slice for question 1 of #2603 (M29 before G84). Question 2 (G73 or G83, the R plane) still waits for the machine owner.

## Cause

On a 30i/31i/32i control, G84 is rigid without M29 only when parameter 5200 bit 0 is set. The post wrote no M29. A control without that setting needs `M29 S..` before G84. The owner has not said which setting his 31i-A5 has, so the post gets an option.

## Tests

New file `crates/post/tests/fanuc_rigid_tap.rs`:

- `fanuc_rigid_tap_m29_is_off_by_default`: no M29 when the option is not set.
- `fanuc_rigid_tap_m29_precedes_each_g84_group`: three G84 groups, each with `M29 S600` on the block before it, and no M29 on the drill operation.
- `fanuc_rigid_tap_m29_without_spindle_speed_is_refused_by_name`: a tap with no spindle speed is refused by name, with no M29 and no G84.
- `fanuc_rigid_tap_m29_option_is_declared_off`: the option is declared with the default `false`.

Mutation results:

- Unchanged post: `..._precedes_each_g84_group` and `..._option_is_declared_off` fail (red). The default test passes, as expected.
- Speed guard disabled: `..._without_spindle_speed_is_refused_by_name` fails (red). Restored: all four pass.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 120 steps, 0 failed. The steps are all the post suites and the app suites that read `fanuc.cps`, including `conformance`, `rigid_tapping` and `posting`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `fanuc_aicc` (7 tests) still passes.

## Goldens moved

None. The option is off by default. Every golden stays byte-identical.

## Not exercised

- No run on a real control. The owner's 31i-A5 graphic check is the next step when the option is on.
- No heavy lanes run. The diff reaches no geometry or motion code.

## Overlaps

- #3441 touches `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` in `declaredOptions` and in `onCycle` (one line, the `aiccOff()` call that is already on main). It does not change the G84 or G99 lines that this PR changes. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/2603-fanuc-m29.md`.

Changelog: Fanuc post: a new option, "Rigid tap M29 before G84" (off by default), writes `M29 S<rpm>` before each G84 cycle group for a control that taps rigid only after M29.

Refs #2603

title: fix(post): keep a repeated tool in the grbl-family posts
body:
## What changed

- `grblhal.cps`, `grbl.cps` and `tinyg.cps` remember the tool that the program last loaded (`loadedTool`). This is the rule that `tormach.cps` has since #1626.
- When the next section asks for the same tool, the post writes no tool change:
  - grblHAL: no `T<n> M6`, and no optional `M1` before it.
  - TinyG: no `M5` / `M9` / `T<n> M6` / `M0` block, and no frame restate after it.
  - Grbl 1.1: no `TOOL CHANGE - LOAD` comment and no `M0`.
- A program stop or an optional stop after an operation makes the tool unknown again. The operator can take the tool out at a stop.
- The tool comment, the Z lift, the section-end `M5` / `M9`, the next `S.. M3` and the Z-only clearance rapid before the first traverse stay.

## Cause

The three posts wrote a full tool change for each `TOOL` record. The stream sends a `TOOL` record for each section, also when the tool does not change. On a manual-change router, each `M6` (or the Grbl `M0`) halts the program.

## Tests

- New file `crates/post/tests/grbl_family_same_tool.rs`, six tests:
  - `grblhal_repeated_tool_writes_one_tool_change`
  - `grblhal_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again`
  - `grbl_repeated_tool_writes_no_tool_change_stop`
  - `grbl_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again`
  - `tinyg_repeated_tool_writes_one_tool_change`
  - `tinyg_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again`
- All six were red on unchanged code.
- Mutations:
  - `grblhal.cps` from upstream/main: the two grblhal tests are red.
  - `grbl.cps` from upstream/main: the two grbl tests are red.
  - `tinyg.cps` from upstream/main: the two tinyg tests are red.
  - The grblHAL stop reset removed: `grblhal_new_tool_return_and_stop_each_change_again` is red.
  - Restored: all six are green.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 58 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. No recorded stream or app golden has two sections in a row on one tool for these posts.

## Not exercised

- No real grblHAL, Grbl or TinyG controller.
- The q07 router project was not posted again through the app.
- The Z lift and the spindle stop and start between same-tool sections stay. The issue asks for them to go too. `docs/decisions/3445-grbl-same-tool.md` says why they stay.

## Overlaps

None.

Changelog: The grblHAL, Grbl 1.1 and TinyG posts write no tool change between operations that keep the same tool.

Fixes #3445

title: fix(trace): protect selected faces and edges along the full tool sweep
body:
Replacement for #3389. GitHub closed the original draft when the base branch of #3352 was deleted after merge. Main contains that parent. The original draft used commit `abed47739`. A trial merge with main at `6679b1b4b` was clean. The eight-file change on that tree has the same patch ID as the original change. On the trial merge `4afe34f02`, all five app `do_not_touch` tests and all six matching UI tests passed. They include the full tool sweep, tilted Trace refusal, blocked post, and viewport selection.

Trace now accepts protected faces and edges. Generation checks the full tool along the selected line, including links and plunges. If a move cannot keep the requested clearance, generation refuses it and names the protected item. The post gate checks current protected geometry again. A Trace without protected items keeps its original moves.

## Review fixes on `3980979a2`

I merged upstream `main` at `6e641dac7` into the branch. Both reported failures reproduced on merge commit `d5353abf3`. The generated MCP reference was out of date. The click test could not arm the protected picker after the Geometry panel grew taller.

I regenerated the reference with `camcraft-cli mcp reference`. The test now scrolls each control into view before it clicks. On the updated head, all six `mcp_doc_drift` tests and all three `do_not_touch_click` tests passed. The quick and release gates for this head are in progress.

## Screenshots

**Trace Geometry before** (`6e641dac7`)

![Trace Geometry before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/59db5a8401816032f74ef0791c3535d5823e2fe6/3462/3462-trace-before-main-6e641dac7.png)

**Verification on `abed47739`**

- `trace_protects_the_full_sweep_between_clear_endpoints` failed on the parent when MCP refused protected items on Trace. It passes on this head.
- The test places a protected face between two clear endpoints. The holder reaches it at a distance of 14.9 mm with a 15 mm clearance envelope. The shank reaches it at 6.9 mm with a 7 mm envelope. The clear case keeps the original moves. A refused path writes no NC file.
- `tilted_trace_refuses_a_protected_face_in_its_work_plane` passes.
- `trace_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click` passes with actual viewport clicks.

title: feat(motion): engrave and trace open and closed sketch chains
body:
Engrave and Trace now follow open and closed chains from a placed sketch. The user can select a profile, individual chains or a layer. The operation preserves the cut direction of lines, arcs and circles. It applies the sketch placement and the work-coordinate rotation to both endpoints and arc centers. A lift separates disconnected strokes and gaps accepted by the drawing tolerance.

Each depth level approaches from the stock surface. The existing stock, fixture, shank and mark-depth checks can hold the post, including jobs that have no part solid. Very short arcs below the post resolution give a diagnostic. A major arc is split into two arcs that keep its center and sweep. #3442 tracks the separate case where a native Fanuc post accepts a short arc supplied directly in an intermediate file.

The 18-move CL fixture contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes.

## Verification

- On the parent source, `placed_sketch_marks_keep_open_and_closed_arcs_and_retract_between_strokes` failed because an operation could not use picked sketch chains. The same test passed on this fix. The original CLI also refused both Engrave and Trace on a whole profile.

The native CLI generated, verified and posted six synthetic drawings across both operations. Short representable arcs kept distinct endpoints. The 270-degree and near-full sweeps used split arcs with the correct centers. Both sub-resolution cases gave a named refusal and wrote no NC file.

title: fix(motion): honor the Circular ring order and protect each entry
body:
This change depends on #3353. The PR now targets `main` so that deleting the parent branch will keep this review open. Integration commit `03929655b` joins the shared pass-start change with current main. Main includes #3113, which protects the move between Circular rings. The [Circular-only comparison](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/03929655b86b9a7b8e3dab176063a10fa621747b...c9b1ed4a65325c5dcaedc9369f4d9e55264c029b) starts at that integration commit.

Circular now accepts Auto, Inside, and Outside in its Passes tab and through MCP. A saved project omits Auto. Inside cuts the smallest ring first. Outside cuts the largest ring first. Auto keeps the existing order, curved-floor depth sequence and CL output.

For a flat 10 mm radius pocket, a 6 mm cutter and a 2 mm stepover, the tool-center radii are 1, 3, 5 and 7 mm. Inside visits them in that order. Outside visits 7, 5, 3 and 1 mm. The tool completes the selected depth levels and lifts vertically to clearance before it crosses to the next ring.

On a curved floor, forced passes start their depth steps at stock height. The tool stays inside the current ring during entry. The checks cover the full helical orbit and its rounded endpoints. A short entry that cannot produce a valid arc uses the existing named fallback. The phase check uses the actual orbit on the outer ring when Inside approaches the rim.

title: fix(2d): Pass starts at Inside/Outside cuts level curves of the start side
body:
Stacked on #3353 (merge #3353 first).

This PR is the review fix of #3353 that the second read asked for (comment 7077845657 on #3353). I could not push to the #3353 branch, so it comes as a stacked PR. It keeps everything of #3353 (the type, the field, the project key, the MCP door, the UI row and its pins). It replaces only the ring law of Inside and Outside.

## What changed

- New modules `crates/motion/src/machining2d/sided_rings.rs` (the rings) and `sided_chain.rs` (the passes and lead-ins). Inside and Outside no longer sort the closed rings of the area. Ring `j` is now a level curve of the START SIDE alone:
  - Outside: the outer loop filled and eroded by `j` stepovers.
  - Inside: the holes filled and grown by `j` stepovers.
  - The parts of ring `j` in the area are open pieces that end on the far wall. Ring `j` is cut before ring `j + 1`. The far wall loops are cut last, whole.
- Each component of the area (an outer loop with its holes) is planned alone. Inside on a component with no hole keeps the core-first order.
- Climb keeps the uncut material on the right (#1555). The far wall ring uses the Auto ring law.
- A new pass starts with a short lead-in from a piece that this level already cut (at most 1.5 stepovers). The entry then lands in a cleared column, not on the part wall in uncut stock.
- Open pieces stop 50 um short of the far wall. Without this, the micron lattice put piece ends a hair across the wall ring, and the verifier reported 141 feed crossings on fig8.
- Refusals by name: a piece with an inner vertex outside the area, and a hole with no enclosing outer loop.
- Auto: `waterline_passes` is back to the `upstream/main` text, byte for byte. `PassStart::rank` is removed.
- `start_wall_note` (motion) and one line in `generate.rs`: a level that must start on a wall gets a toolpath note. This is Inside on an area with a hole, or Outside where the outer boundary is in the stock (a closed pocket).
- Texts corrected: the decision file, the UI hint, and the guide no longer say "no ring is a full slot" for all cases. They name the start-on-a-wall case.

## Cause

The rank of #3353 sorted whole closed loops by winding. After a band splits, one piece loop has arcs on the stock side and arcs on the part side. The part-side arcs then cut uncut stock on both sides: a full slot. No order of closed loops can fix this. The level curves of one side do not have the problem.

## Tests

Pins (red on the #3353 head 59b42c727, green now):
- `pass_start_engagement::outside_on_a_split_band_never_slots`. Red text: `climb true: Outside cuts 8.03 mm wide near Point2 { x: 22.34161637316847, y: -5.446639271441037 }`. It is the 100 x 40 / radius 15 band of the second read. A 0.25 mm material grid measures the worst width of cut over any 3 tool radii of floor feed. Limit: 1.5 stepovers. It also checks that no stock is left off the part wall.
- `pass_start_engagement::outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock`: red on #3353 (52.75 mm2 of stock cut by later entries).
- `offset_pass_start::fig8_outside_offset_never_slots_along_a_level` (fig8.step, EM-0800-4FL, the maintainer's heights). It checks the width along each level, no `Crossing` warning, and no start-wall note on the band.

Other new tests: `outside_on_a_figure_eight_band_never_slots`, `inside_on_the_band_clears_the_whole_band`, `auto_on_the_band_slots_so_the_measure_sees_a_slot` (the measure sees a slot), and the unit test `pass_start::tests::a_start_on_a_wall_is_named_and_a_start_in_air_is_not`.

Mutations (each red, then green after the restore):
1. The #3353 planner files back: `outside_on_a_split_band_never_slots` red (8.03 mm), `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` red (52.75 mm2).
2. Lead-in switched off: `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` red (321.38 mm2).
3. End trim set to 0: `fig8_outside_offset_never_slots_along_a_level` red (`141 feed crossings, first Some("Crossing { moves: [36, 1654] }")`).

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 386 steps, 0 failed (47.1 min). It ran on the tree before the last change. That change moved the chain code from `sided_rings.rs` to `sided_chain.rs` for the 400-line law, with no change to the logic.
- After that move: `pass_start_engagement` (5 tests), the `pass_start` unit test and `offset_pass_start` (4 tests) pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens moved

None. Auto is unchanged: `waterscan.rs` has no diff to `upstream/main`.

## Not exercised

- The heavy lanes (release, `--ignored`) did not run. "Not run" is not a pass.
- Outside with "Do not touch" picks (`pocket_avoid_started`) has no test.
- Inside has no engagement pin: its first ring is on the part wall, which is a full-width cut by design. The note names it.
- A part with a deep concave notch that faces away from the start side. The fig8 waist is covered.
- `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` is not changed. My session could not edit it. Its claim ("with an Outside containment the stock edge, so no ring slots the stock") is true with this fix.

## Overlaps

- #3353: the same functions (`plan_passes_from`, `PassStart`, the 2D Offset arm of `generate.rs`). This PR is stacked on it.

Changelog: 2D Offset "Pass starts at" Inside/Outside cut level curves of the start side, so a split band never cuts a full-width slot; each new pass leads in from cut stock, and a start on a wall is named in the toolpath notes.

Refs #1448
Fixes #3316

title: fix(ui): explain the fixed Trochoidal Slot loop order
body:
Stacked on #3401. That PR uses the locked Passes row from #3387, which follows #3353. The GitHub base is the upstream branch of #3353. Commit `4ab08d8ea` contains only the Trochoidal Slot change.

Trochoidal Slot shows a disabled Auto control and explains the loop order. The tool starts at the entry bore. Each new loop advances along the slot and uses clearance from the preceding cut. The MCP add and edit commands give the same reason when a caller supplies `pass_start`. A saved Trochoidal Slot keeps its existing format.

For a straight slot, the entry bore is at the start of the chain. At one cutting depth, the next loop centers advance by one accepted spacing along the chain. title: fix(multiaxis): state the rotaries before the first tilted feed
body:
## Cause

A 5-axis stamp path left its opening moves (before the first lean) without a pose. The post dump commanded zero angles only for a Z column after a lean. So the first move that the Fanuc post wrote with rotary words was the first tilted feed. The Fanuc angle memory (`rotAt`, `assets/posts/fanuc.cps`) was null, and the rate guard (`rotaryFeed`) refused the feed on `tilthead.mch` (A and B rates stated):

```text
a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held
```

## Fix (two sites, both small)

1. `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs`: when a path leans anywhere, each station before the first lean states the upright Z column (`Some(UP)`). A path that never leans stays silent, as before.
2. `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` (`dump`): in a stream that leans, the first move that states the Z column commands explicit zero angles. Before, the zero came only after a lean.

Why both: the stamp alone does not help, because the dump wrote nothing for a stated Z column before a lean (the released claim on #3300 found this). The dump alone (zero on any first move) would guess an upright home for a move that states nothing. The guard forbids that guess. With the two parts, the post commands only a pose that the stream states. The rate guard is unchanged. A stream with no pose before its first tilted feed still refuses.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/3300-opening-rotary-pose.md` (chosen, why, dropped).

## Opening blocks (Fanuc, tilthead.mch, 5-Axis Contour on the cap, clearance 20 mm, G54 at Z 50)

| Before (origin/main) | After (this PR) |
|---|---|
| post refused: `a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held` (no program) | `G43.4 H01` |
| | `G00 Z-30.` |
| | `G00 X0. Y-3.84 Z-30. A0. B0.` |
| | `G01 X-0.776 Y-3.149 Z-47.314 A13.313 B15.42 F100` |

By the code (not posted in a test), main writes the same blocks without `A0. B0.` on a machine with no stated rate. The rotation then starts from an unknown angle. The order is: TCP on, retract to the clearance, the XY rapid at the clearance with A0 B0, then the approach. Flow5D: `G00 X-2.142 Y-6.642 Z-30. A0. B0.`. Swarf: `G00 X-24. Y-10.149 Z-25. A0. B0.`.

Note: the approach feed (the G01 above) turns the rotaries while it descends to the first contact. That is the stamp's existing pose law, and it is not changed here. Filed as #3414 for a decision.

## Tests (red on main, green here)

- `camcraft-post` `opening_rotary_pose`:
  - `a_leaning_stream_commands_zero_angles_on_its_first_upright_move`: red without the dump change (`no refusal: ["a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held"]`), green with it.
  - `a_stream_with_no_pose_before_its_first_tilted_feed_still_refuses`: the guard. A prismatic opening and a feed-first stream still refuse by name. Green before and after.
  - `an_upright_stream_that_never_leans_commands_no_angles`: a stream that states only the Z column posts byte-identical to a stream with no axis, without G43.4.
- `camcraft-app` `opening_rotary_pose` (generate on `tilthead.mch` + post with `fanuc.cps`):
  - `contour5d_opening_states_rotaries_before_the_fanuc_tilted_feed`

title: fix(2d): keep Face rows clear of 'Do not touch' items
body:
## What changed

- A Face operation now accepts "Do not touch" picks. The Boundary group of the Geometry tab shows "Pick protected" for a Face operation.
- At each cut level, the Face generator gets the cutter-centre keep-out of the protected items. The keep-out covers flutes, shank and holder, plus the clearance, for each tip height from the level up to the clearance plane.
- The generator cuts each row short at the keep-out. It uses the same interval law that clips rows at bridged holes (`face_holes::pieces`).
- Where a row is cut short, or where a row-end step (sharp or blended) crosses the keep-out, the facer links over the keep-out at the clearance plane: up, across, plunge.
- The existing rapid router raises a link that must go higher. The existing `verify_avoid` check and the post gate read every Face move.
- A level with no row left is skipped. A path note tells this.
- When no level is left, the generator refuses the operation and names the protected items. The post is blocked.
- A path note tells that the material beside the protected items stays unfaced.
- Without protected items, the Face path is the same as before, move for move.
- The refusal text for an unsupported kind and the MCP tool text now name Face.

New code:
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/face_keep.rs`: the per-level clip, the step test and the notes.
- `machining2d::face_over_kept` and `machining2d::FaceKeep`. `face_over` calls `face_over_kept` with `None`.

## Cause

`do_not_touch_applies` held only 2D Offset and 3D Pocket. The Face generator did not read the protected items.

## Tests

Pins:
- `crates/app/tests/do_not_touch_face.rs`
  - `face_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face`: a Face at Cut Z 20 runs over a tower. With the tower top protected (clearance 1.5 mm), no sample of any move below the tower top comes nearer than 4.5 mm (flute radius 3 + 1.5). Verify is clean. The post writes NC.
  - `face_do_not_touch_refuses_an_impossible_cut_by_name_and_blocks_the_post`: the plate top is protected with a 16 mm clearance. Generate refuses with "Do not touch" and "plate" in the text. The post is refused and writes no file.
  - `face_without_protection_keeps_its_toolpath`: protection changes the path. After undo of the protection, the path is the same as the first path, move for move.
- `crates/motion/tests/face_keep.rs`
  - `empty_keepout_is_face_over_to_the_byte` (4 cases: sharp, blended, single level, staged).
  - `rows_and_steps_keep_out_of_the_keepout_and_link_over_it` (sharp and blended).
  - `a_keepout_over_every_row_refuses_by_name`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`
  - `face_op_shows_pick_protected_button` (new).
  - `unsupported_op_shows_do_not_touch_note_without_pick_button`: the note text now names Face.

Red before the fix: both app pins failed on `upstream/main` 174584111 with `'Do not touch' is supported on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket operations only so far - clear it on Face`.

Mutations (each one red, then green after restore):
- Remove the `step_clear` guard in `face.rs`: `rows_and_steps_keep_out_of_the_keepout_and_link_over_it` fails.
- Make `face_keep::level` ignore the keep-out: two motion pins fail.
- Pass `None` for the keep-out in `generate.rs`: all three app pins fail. (Verify finds the avoid hit, so the safety net blocks the post too.)

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 280 steps, 0 failed (`ui suites: lib` 1425 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Heavy lanes

- Head: `b38f0c12f33ec6b2e1c8e0ea7d59c20c74130db4` (unchanged; no merge or code push).
- Base: `upstream/main` at `054c1e24bb15f27fee5f022ab454384c951e8e64`, fetched before the run.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 242 steps, 0 failed. Exit 0.
- Lanes: 1 release build, 37 motion heavy steps, 204 app heavy steps.
- Four known-fail checks were red as expected. The tool counted them as OK: #1950 (three checks), #2849 (one check).
- App heavy included `example_catalog` and `golden_cl`. These ran with the heavy lane's ignored-test selection.
- The worktree is clean. No code, golden or recorded program changed.
- No new pin or mutation was needed. This round had no code findings. The reviewed pins and mutation results above still apply.
- This round did not repeat quick, clippy or the regular debug catalog suite. The requested work was the owed heavy run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A Face laid along an open boundary (a turned frame) with protected items. The keep-out turns with the region, but no test covers it.
- A tilted (3+2) Face with protected items.
- A protected edge chain on a Face (the app pin uses a face pick).

## Overlaps

- #2831 (draft, `needs-rework`, `conflicts`) changes other lines of the Face arm in `generate.rs` (the `blend_radius` field). It touches the same file, different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.
- Several open PRs touch `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` and `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs` in other functions or other lines.

## Decision

`docs/decisions/3343-face-do-not-touch.md`.

title: fix(2d): Pass starts at (Auto/Inside/Outside) for 2D Adaptive
body:
Stacked on #3353 (merge #3353 first).

## What changed

- 2D Adaptive has the shared `pass_start` field of #3316. It uses the same type, the same project key, the same Passes-tab row and the same MCP door (`edit_operation`). There is no new type.
- `auto` is never written to the file. The digest writes the value only off Auto. Every earlier operation keeps its cache stamp.
- The planner of the Spiral method reads the field (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_hsm_start.rs`):
  - **Auto**: the plan of every earlier file. The planner does not read the stock outline.
  - **Outside**: the #1950 air plan cuts each piece from the air past the stock edge inward. If a piece has no air side, the HSM plan is refused (`hsm_passes` with `air_only`). Then the Offset rings cut the area from its outer edge in. The note names the switch.
  - **Inside**: in a pocket without holes, the growth plan starts in the core and grows out. This is the Inside order. In an area with holes, the Offset rings cut from the hole wall out. The note names the switch.
  - The trochoid fallback runs only under Auto. Each ring fallback uses the selected order.
- The Trochoidal method refuses Inside and Outside by name. The refusal is at the command door (`named_refusal`), in the generator, and in a consequence line under the row.
- The generator gives the stock outline to the planner only for an untilted operation (the outline is in world XY).
- The user guide (`operations-2d.md`) describes the option for 2D Adaptive.

## Cause

2D Adaptive had no pass order option. On an Outside band, its plan could not start at the stock edge (#2849 pin 3, the fig8 case).

## Tests

Pins (red before the fix, green after):
- `adaptive_pass_start::fig8_outside_adaptive_starts_in_air_and_ends_on_the_part_wall`: red before (`the first pass starts 0.000 mm outside the stock`).
- `adaptive_pass_start::fig8_inside_adaptive_starts_on_the_part_wall_and_ends_in_air`: red before (`the first pass starts 23.917 mm from the part`).
- `adaptive_pass_start::trochoidal_adaptive_refuses_a_forced_pass_start_by_name`: red before (the Trochoidal method cut the path).
- `adaptive_pass_start::mcp_sets_adaptive_pass_start_and_undo_restores_it`: MCP, undo and the project file.
- `machining2d::pocket_hsm_start::tests::*` (6 tests in motion): the air plan path on a sketch band, Outside without a stock outline, Outside on a closed pocket, Inside with holes, Inside without holes equal to Auto, and Auto equal with and without the stock outline (byte for byte).
- `egui_app::tests::pass_start::the_adaptive_twin_offers_pass_start_and_says_the_trochoidal_refusal`: replaces `the_adaptive_twin_has_no_pass_start_row_yet`, which pinned the absence of the row. The `#[test]` count does not change.

Mutations (each made red, then restored and green):
1. `pocket.rs`: the old call `adaptive_passes(center, p, "this pocket", true, None)` -> the fig8 Outside and Inside pins are red.
2. `pocket_hsm.rs`: the `air_only` guard off -> `outside_on_a_closed_pocket_rides_the_rings_from_its_wall_said` is red.
3. `pocket_hsm_start.rs`: the Inside-with-holes arm off -> `inside_with_holes_starts_on_the_part_wall_said` is red.
4. `generate.rs`: the Trochoidal refusal off -> the Trochoidal pin is red (`the Trochoidal method cut a forced order`).
5. `sane.rs`: the Trochoidal refusal off -> the Trochoidal pin is red (`the command door refuses`).

Gate:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 386 of 387 steps were green. The red step was `params_files_stay_under_the_line_law`, because `params.rs` had 404 lines. The fix (commit `addb167c2`) moves the pass-start digest bytes into `digest::write_pass_start`, which Offset and Adaptive share. The bytes do not change. After the fix, `app lib` is green (297 tests).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Heavy lanes that ran (release, `--ignored`), all green: `motion heavy: adaptive_hsm`, `motion heavy: pocket3d_hsm`, `app heavy: golden_cl`, `app heavy: solid_law_goldens`, `app heavy: roughing2d`, `app heavy: shoulder_adaptive`, `app heavy: adaptive_pass_start`, `app heavy: offset_pass_start`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` lists 243 reached steps, because a `motion` change reaches every `app` heavy lane. The other 235 steps did not run. "Not run" is not a pass. The full heavy run is necessary before this PR is flagged ready.

## Goldens moved

None. Auto does not read the new input. A motion pin compares the Auto path with and without the stock outline.

## Not exercised

- On fig8, the Outside containment band stops where the tool's disc touches the stock. The air plan puts its entry 0.005 mm (`AIR_GAP`) further out. So on fig8, Outside uses the Outside rings, and the note says so. The air plan path is pinned on a sketch band that reaches past the stock (motion test). The decision file records this finding.
- A tilted 2D Adaptive with Outside (it uses the rings, and the note says "no stock outline"). No pin.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row for 2D Adaptive. This session could not edit `.claude/skills/` (the edit was blocked). The row of #3353 says "Other kinds get the same key in their own issues". A follow-up adds the 2D Adaptive sentence.
- The `#2849` known-fail pin (`shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`) uses Auto. It stays known-fail.

## Overlaps

- Stacked on #3353 (`pocket.rs`, `generate.rs`, `kind_editors.rs`, `mill2d_page.rs`, `pass_start_row.rs`, the project params). This PR extends the functions that #3353 adds.
- #2890 (draft, `needs-rework`) adds a `rest` field to the same `OpParams::Adaptive2D` variant and its match arms. It touches the same file, different field lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #3283, #3251, #3058, #3103, #3115, #3059 touch `generate.rs`, `params.rs` or `sane.rs` in other arms. #3378 touches `sane.rs` in a different function.

Decision: `docs/decisions/3355-adaptive-pass-start.md`.

Changelog: 2D Adaptive has "Pass starts at" (Auto / Inside / Outside): Outside cuts an open band from the air past the stock edge (or Offset rings from the outer edge, said in the notes); Inside grows from the core of a pocket (or Offset rings from the island or part wall); Trochoidal refuses Inside and Outside by name.

title: fix(slot): explain the fixed pass order for a groove
body:
This PR depends on #3387 and #3353. The GitHub base is now `main` to preserve this review when the parent branch is deleted. Commit `3572ca334` contains only the Slot change.

The Slot Passes tab shows a disabled Auto row and explains why a radial order has no meaning here. A tool-width groove has one centreline. A wider groove connects neighbouring rows and finishes along its wall. Each connected pass must keep its cutting sequence. The MCP add and edit paths now explain this when a caller supplies `pass_start`. No Slot field is stored. The planner keeps its original output.

**Hand trace.** For a 10 mm groove, a 4 mm cutter, a 0.5 mm allowance at each wall, and a 2 mm stepover, the offsets are -2.5, -0.5, +1.5, and +2.5 mm. The tool traverses consecutive rows in opposite directions. Each link joins adjacent ends. The wall lap starts at the end of the last row.

title: feat(app): saved cut recipes - apply an operation's settings to new geometry
body:
## What changed

Saved cut recipes hold an operation's parameters, its tool name, and its workpiece material. A user library stores them in `recipes.camrecipes`, with a `camcraft-recipes/1` envelope. The folder is `CAMCRAFT_RECIPES`, else `<platform data dir>/camcraft/recipes`.

`ApplyCutRecipe` wraps `CreateOperation`. One undo removes the new operation. MCP tools `save_cut_recipe`, `list_cut_recipes`, and `apply_cut_recipe` use this library. Each tool accepts an optional `library` path. The generated MCP reference and the guide list the tools.

The caller supplies the new source. The command refuses a recipe by name if its saved parameters contain geometry that the API cannot replace. The audit covers:

- Drill holes and cross holes; bore and thread holes.
- Contour chain overrides and excluded deburr edges.
- Tilted plane origins.
- Circular centers, slot endpoints, probe targets, and undercut endpoints.
- Wire start and sync points; sinker burn positions.

The command also refuses a missing tool, an unknown material, and a material mismatch. When a recipe names a material, the destination must have that material in force. An absent destination material now causes a refusal with the recipe name.

The library format stays the same. The decision record is `docs/decisions/3073-cut-recipes.md`.

## Review fixes and pin proof

The review found two defects. Applying a recipe copied geometry from its previous source. The material check also accepted an absent destination material.

Regression pins in `crates/app/tests/cut_recipe/safety.rs`:

- `cut_recipe_does_not_transfer_holes_to_a_different_source`: transfer between plates with holes at different coordinates.
- `cut_recipe_refuses_other_saved_coordinates_by_name`: other operations with saved coordinates.
- `cut_recipe_refuses_saved_picks_and_plane_origins`: cross holes, entity picks, and tilted plane origins.
- `cut_recipe_with_a_named_material_requires_a_destination_material`: command refusal when the destination material is absent.
- `cut_recipe_mcp_refuses_an_absent_destination_material`: MCP refusal for the same case.

The four original tests in `crates/app/tests/cut_recipe.rs` also cover save, load, apply, generation, undo, and the existing refusals.

Mutation evidence: Removing the geometry guard made all three geometry pins fail. Restoring the old material guard made both absent-material pins fail. After restoration, all nine recipe tests passed. The final quick gate ran the restored pins again.

## Final validation

Head: `e8eb8429461c63a4df20d11dca24e0a71582c34f`
Base: `upstream/main`, fetched for this gate at `6e641dac753020bfed49fec310237eed28448141`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 337 steps, 2,666 tests passed, zero failures, 22 ignored (36.6 minutes).
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 206 steps, zero gate failures, 46 tests passed (28.2 minutes). Two registered known-fail tests failed as expected; the gate accepted these results: `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level` (#1950) and `shoulder_adaptive::fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works` (#2849).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `app suites: example_catalog`: GREEN. 37 tests passed, four ignored (18.58 seconds). This suite ran in the quick gate. Heavy step 53 ran the four ignored cases; all passed. Combined catalog result: 41 of 41 passed.
- `mcp_doc_drift`: GREEN.
- Other reached golden suites: GREEN. All 27 reached suites with direct golden checks passed: `adaptive_trochoid`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_post_inch`, `lathe_post_thread_dips`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `pocket_no_adaptive`, `pocket3d_trochoid`, `probe_op`, `program_entry`, `rest_pocket`, `sinker_burn`, `sinker_orbit`, `sinker_side`, `sinker_undersize`, `sinker_wear`, `slot_dxf_sketch`, `thread_boss`, `thread_mill`, `v_carve_op`, `wear_comp`, `contour_start_point`, `control_comp`, `corner_relief`, and `first_router_part`.

## Goldens moved

None. After the catalog suite ran, no recorded program or golden file changed.

## Not exercised

- The first quick run hit seeded-artifact error `E0463`. An isolated target clean and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1` resolved it. The final quick run passed.
- UI screenshots do not apply. This PR changes no UI files.
- There is no GUI recipe panel. Issue #3393 holds that work.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill has no row for the new tools. This PR supplies the generated reference and guide entries.
- Recipes omit coolant and area controls. Coolant depends on the machine. Area controls depend on the geometry.
- Automatic geometry matching is not exercised. The command refuses recipes that need replacement geometry.
- The knowledge graph could not be updated because `graphify` is not installed on this host.

Effort: high

Changelog: Saved cut recipes: save an operation's settings under a name and apply them to new geometry in one undoable step (MCP `save_cut_recipe`, `list_cut_recipes`, `apply_cut_recipe`); a recipe whose tool or material is gone is refused by name.

Fixes #3073

title: feat(release): optionally sign and notarize the macOS packages
body:
The macOS packaging step can sign the app and its three executables with Developer ID. It can submit the app and the DMG to the Apple notary service. It staples the app before it makes the final ZIP. It staples and validates the DMG before publishing either archive.

With no signing inputs, the packager keeps the ad hoc path and reports it. An incomplete set of inputs stops packaging. The release workflow passes the five optional secrets only to the packaging step. A private temporary keychain holds the certificate. The script removes temporary credentials on exit. The release triggers and permissions stay the same.

## Verification

On commit `e536469d0`, all five packaging fixture tests passed, including six simulated failure cases. `test_signed_zip_and_dmg_include_validated_tickets` checks the two archives. `test_partial_signing_settings_fail_before_packaging` checks incomplete inputs. The original script failed nine fixture assertions. Shell parsing, release workflow YAML parsing, the five secret mappings, and the commit whitespace check passed.

A second test used native macOS tools and three small universal Mach-O programs. It extracted the ZIP and mounted the DMG read-only. It verified ad hoc signatures, the arm64 and x86_64 slices of each program, the icon, an example, and the Applications link. This test exposed an incompatible two-architecture lipo check. The final script checks each architecture separately.

## Limits

The Developer ID and notary service tests used simulated credentials and command responses. No production identity, Apple submission, release upload, or hosted workflow ran. A maintainer with the release credentials must confirm Apple's acceptance on a signed build.

Changelog: macOS release packages can use Developer ID signing and Apple notarization when the release credentials are configured.

Effort: medium

Fixes #1642

title: fix(ui): name clearance links when the retract hop is off
body:
Stacked on #3353. The PR base is `issue/3316-offset-pass-start`, as the review permits.
Retarget this PR to `main` BEFORE #3353 merges. Then merge `upstream/main` into this branch and run the gate again.
The base change keeps the old parent code out of this PR's diff.

## What changed

The 2D Offset and 2D Adaptive Lead tab names the effective link plane.

title: feat(text): place typed text in a TrueType outline font as closed shapes
body:
## What changed

- New module `camcraft_geometry::outline_text`. It reads a TrueType outline font and makes a typed string into closed shapes, in mm, on the layer `text`.
  - `ttf.rs` is our own reader, written from the public OpenType specification. It reads `cmap` formats 4 and 12, `loca`, `glyf` (simple and composite glyphs), `hmtx`, `hhea`, `maxp`, `head` and the `OS/2` cap height. Each read has a bounds check.
  - `mod.rs` flattens the quadratic contours to lines, with a chord error of 0.005 mm or less. It then makes a `SketchData` with closed chains only.
  - `sample_font.rs` makes a small test font in memory. It has our own glyphs, so the repository stores no font file.
- New undoable command `InsertOutlineText` (`crates/app/src/commands/insert_outline_text.rs`). It reads the font once at construction. The profile keeps the shapes, not the font, so the project file format does not change.
- New MCP tool `insert_outline_text` (`crates/app/src/mcp/outline_text_tools.rs`). The tool is also in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (generated) and in the MCP guide table.
- These inputs are refused by name:
  - a font that cannot be read, a CFF font (`.otf` with PostScript outlines) or a font collection;
  - an empty text, or a character that the font does not have;
  - outlines that cross or touch;
  - a height or a spacing outside the limits;
  - a setup that does not exist, a setup with no stock, or a name that is in use.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3072-outline-text.md`.

## Cause

This is a new feature (#3072). Before this PR, typed text was only single-stroke engraving text (`insert_text`, #2679).

## Review fixes

- Large curves keep the 0.005 mm chord tolerance. A curve can use up to 4096 pieces. A curve that needs more is refused.
- Composite glyphs apply `SCALED_COMPONENT_OFFSET`. A component with both offset flags is refused.
- Table reads use each declared table boundary. Character maps also use each declared subtable boundary.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test outline_text`: 9 passed after the fixes.
- Pin proof: the new tests remained in place while the original reviewed source replaced the fixes. All four new tests failed. The restored fixes passed all 9 tests.
  - `large_curves_measure_inside_the_chord_tolerance`: at height 1000 mm, the old code exceeded 0.005 mm. The test measures curve-to-chord distance.
  - `composite_offsets_use_the_component_transform`: the old code gave minimum `(1.0, 3.6)` mm. The test requires `(0.5, 1.8)` mm.
  - `declared_table_lengths_bound_reads_with_trailing_bytes`: the old code accepted a declared `head` length of zero.
  - `declared_cmap_subtable_lengths_bound_reads`: the old code accepted a short format 4 subtable. A separate mutation bypassed the format 12 length check and failed this test. Both restorations passed.

Final head: `46c7c9ecc33eb92808c572006775a8a8828addf5`. The quick gate ran against `upstream/main` `c484dd3d13b73259fff412e566db52f06e625a39`.

The shared `upstream/main` reference advanced to `ef157211438104997fc9e51f7e3affc4db303545` during the heavy release build. Heavy dry runs against both bases selected the same 242 steps, in the same order. The actual heavy run was initially planned against `c484dd3d13b73259fff412e566db52f06e625a39`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **RED**. The run took 49.1 minutes. Of 1086 steps, 1081 passed and 5 failed.
  - `blind_slot_pocket_family_cuts_from_end_wall_to_stock_edge` and `adaptive2d_spiral_and_offset2d_support_relief_while_trochoidal_and_do_not_touch_refuse` failed.
  - `ui suites: lib` failed: 1418 passed, 8 failed and 7 ignored. One failure was `egui_app::post_dialog_tests::desktop_post_command_opens_dialog_and_applies_declared_script_options_undoably`; seven failures reported no graphics adapter.
  - `ui suites: egui_app` failed three headless CLI tests. `ui suites: shell` failed one headless CLI test.
  - The original PR body records the two non-UI failures and the desktop-post failure as pre-existing. This round did not run an independent baseline comparison.
  - These failures limit verification. The full quick gate is red.
- Clippy: **GREEN**, 111 seconds. Command: `cargo clippy -j4 -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- The geometry outline suite passed all 9 tests. The app outline suite passed all 4 tests.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: **GREEN**, 34.2 minutes. All 242 reached app and motion steps passed. No step failed. Four known-fail probes failed as expected: three for #1950 and one for #2849.
- The final head and worktree remained unchanged through verification. The latest upstream reference was still `ef157211438104997fc9e51f7e3affc4db303545` at completion.

## Goldens moved

- `app suites: example_catalog`: 37 passed and 4 ignored in quick, 12.64 seconds. The heavy gate passed all 4 ignored cases, 3.42 seconds. All 41 catalog tests ran.
- `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed.
- `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed.
- `golden_cl`: 33 passed, 2.52 seconds.
- No recorded program or golden changed. The final worktree is clean.

## Not exercised

- `graphify update`: the command is not installed on this host.
- UI screenshots: not applicable. This PR changes no UI code.

- Toolpath generation on the text. A toolpath from the chains of any DXF-type profile is not on main yet: #1867 does that work. The test only pins that the pocket and the contour accept the text as closed chains.
- A real third-party font file. The tests use the generated sample font only.
- CFF (`.otf` PostScript) fonts. These are refused by name. A CFF reader can come later as a different issue.
- The UI. This PR adds no dialog. The command is available through MCP.

## Overlaps

- #2924 changes `crates/app/src/mcp/sketch_tools.rs` (`insert_text`). This PR does not touch that file.
- #3304 changes `crates/app/src/commands/insert_text.rs`. This PR does not touch that file. It has its own name helper.
- These PRs touch `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`: #3061, #2999, #2993, #2992, #2981, #2979, #2978 and #2924. Each adds a line to the module list, so the lines are different. The PR that merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Typed text in a TrueType outline font becomes a profile of closed shapes (letter holes included) for a pocket, V-carve or cut-out: MCP tool `insert_outline_text`, one undo step; unreadable or CFF fonts, missing glyphs and overlapping outlines are refused by name.

Fixes #3072
