title: fix(post): block cutting tools at reserved numbers and names
body:
Stacked on #3157 (merge #3157 first)

## What changed

Machine files accept `tooling.reserved` entries.
Each entry reserves a number, a name, or both for `probe` or `tool_setter`.
The reader and validator refuse malformed entries by key.
Stored projects retain the reservations.

New cutting tools skip reserved numbers.
A probe takes a declared probe pocket.
Tool edits and library imports refuse incompatible reserved numbers or names.
Verification and posting also refuse old unsafe assignments.
The existing GUI, script, and MCP commands use these checks.
Tool number zero remains refused.

The standalone post CLI checks its input before it creates or replaces output.
It retains the loaded tool across sections.
A new TOOL needs its own declared kind.
A stream with no tool selector cannot post motion on a machine with reservations.
Indexed lookups keep the checks bounded for long streams.

The 18 shipped Tormach mill and router files reserve T99 for the probe.
A machine that omits the field reserves nothing.

## Cause

Tool allocation considered only document numbers.
Machine files could not protect a probe pocket or a control-managed tool name.
The app and standalone post paths had no reservation check.

## Before and after screenshots

These captures are reused from parent #3157.
Both captures use the seeded shell at 1280 × 720 with the HAAS VF-2 machine file mounted.
The camera looks from the front, and the work envelope is shown.
The before capture has "Show operator side" off.
The after capture has the switch on and shows the viewport marker.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![Operator side off](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-before.png) | ![Operator side on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/716acb4411ebb971886b4c98b17eeeb805770f76/2632/operator-side-after.png) |

The images are only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch.

## Tests

### Author-side verification — 2026-11-22

Final head: `757c65cf48a448be98bced1d5565e702e039b622`.
Base at the start of verification: `upstream/main` at `03e05a64991301417bfd17c766fa512c1440950a`.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 150 steps.
The tests reported 2,904 passed, zero failed, and nine ignored.
No step failed. The run took 11.4 minutes.

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 198 steps.
The tests reported 43 passed and four registered known failures.
The gate confirmed all four expected failures. No unexpected failure occurred.
The run took 31.9 minutes.
The change to `crates/app/src/commands/tool.rs` reaches all app heavy targets.
The unchanged final head selects 198 steps. The review trial merge selected 203 steps.

title: feat(multiaxis): Multi-Axis Deburr - tilted chamfer-mill edge breaks with holder tilt-away
body:
## Stock safety fix (current round)

Final head: `ebe55a46f01c774fbdcdcdd49f05205cfb8ec550`.

Multi-Axis Deburr now requires the complete stock boundary to match the source mesh.
Generation and posting refuse missing, empty, non-finite or different stock by name.
The comparison sorts triangle vertices and triangles. It ignores ordering, normals and winding.
Equal bounds do not satisfy the check.

For matching stock, the existing source guard checks the cone, flute, shank and holder through the cut, entry and exit.
Generation also runs the shared `plunge_solid::audit_posed` check.
Posting reads the live stock before it accepts a cached path.
The refusal also applies to a safe different tessellation or stock removed by an earlier operation.
The column simulator still does not judge posed moves. The named refusal prevents an unproved stock verdict from permitting posting.

Pins in `mcp_multiaxis_deburr`:

- `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_stock_beside_the_vertical_edge`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_rechecks_stock_before_posting_the_cached_path`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_live_stock_judge_refuses_an_unjudged_cached_path`.

The clear controls first generate and post source-shaped stock.
The unsafe case adds 60 x 60 x 10 mm stock beside a 40 x 40 x 10 mm part.
The generation pin also sets `center_cutting=true` to isolate the complete-tool guard from the plunge check.
The cached-post pin checks the actual post command after a stock edit. Freshness refuses it and no NC file is written.
The direct live-judge pin checks the named stock refusal independently of freshness.

Pin proof:

- Removing only the generation stock guard makes `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_stock_beside_the_vertical_edge` fail. Generation returns `status: ok`.
- Removing only the live stock guard makes `multiaxis_deburr_live_stock_judge_refuses_an_unjudged_cached_path` fail. The judge returns `None`.
- Restoring both source files byte for byte makes all nine `mcp_multiaxis_deburr` tests pass.

`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test mcp_multiaxis_deburr` passed all nine tests on the final head.

Final-head quick gate:

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 526 steps in 75.3 minutes.
The run had zero failures and zero stalls. It used the merged main revision `deb5364ee`.
Motion library: 551 passed, 10 ignored. App library: 297 passed.
UI library: 1434 passed, 8 ignored. MCP suite: nine passed.
`slot_dxf_sketch`: four passed. No reached golden changed.
The shared `upstream/main` reference advanced to `ef157211` during the run. The tested tree did not change.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the final head in 1 minute 31 seconds.

Final-head heavy gate:

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 244 steps in 58.4 minutes.
The reached lanes were `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. The run had zero failures and zero stalls.
All 108 ordinary ignored tests passed. All four known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
The heavy `example_catalog` suite passed all four tests.
The command used the current `upstream/main` reference after its advance to `ef157211`.
The tested head remained `ebe55a46f01c774fbdcdcdd49f05205cfb8ec550`.

Catalog and goldens on the final head:

- `app suites: example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored, zero failures.
- `app suites: example_catalog_adaptive`: one test passed.
- `app suites: example_catalog_edge_work`: one test passed.
- Goldens moved: none. The catalog suites ran. No recorded program changed in this fix.

The branch includes a clean merge of main as fetched at this round's start: `deb5364ee`.
No conflict required a hand edit. `PROCESS_VERSION` comes from main.
The new exhaustive `pick_kinds` match receives the same `NotTaken(PICK_OWED)` arm as Deburr.
This merge compatibility fix permits the requested current-main build.
This round changes no UI. The existing screenshots still show the current controls.

Changelog: Multi-Axis Deburr refuses stock that lacks a complete posed-tool clearance proof, including changed stock at post.

The earlier sections below record their stated heads. Their validation does not replace this round's validation.

## Separate-part safety fix (earlier round)

Head: `91a03dd8c9d000effb3f4510bd325495a6d22d05`.

Multi-Axis Deburr now refuses by name when another kept part exists. Generation collects the other parts through the shared keep law. Posting checks the live parts before it accepts a cached path. The other parts receive no chamfer exemption. Edge selection stays on the source. This conservative refusal also applies to distant kept parts.

Pins in `mcp_multiaxis_deburr`:
- `multiaxis_deburr_refuses_regeneration_with_a_separate_kept_part`.
- `multiaxis_deburr_rechecks_a_separate_part_before_posting_the_cached_path`.

Each pin uses the review's separate cube and first generates and posts the clear source. The suite passed 6/6. Removing the generation guard, the live posting guard, or the keep-law entry failed the corresponding pins. Each restored source passed. Removing the keep-law entry reproduced the unsafe cached post.

Final-head validation:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 515/516 passed. Only the previously reported stale Slot golden failed in `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size`. No golden changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 242/242 passed. Reached lanes: `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. All 102 ordinary ignored tests passed. All six expected-failure checks matched.

## What changed

- A new operation kind, **Multi-Axis Deburr** (`OpType::MultiAxisDeburr`), is appended at ordinal 46 in `Section::MultiAxis`. Stored kind ids do not move.
- It has every field of the 3D Deburr and five more: `axis_mode` (`Axis5` / `Axis4`), `lead_deg`, `lag_deg`, `max_tilt_deg` and `shank_avoid`.
- New kernel `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::multiaxis_deburr` (`deburr_axis.rs`, `deburr_pose.rs`):
  - The tool lays one cone flank on the chamfer plane of each break. The cut is the flat chamfer for every pose that turns the axis about the plane normal.
  - `Axis5` leans the axis inside `max_tilt_deg`. `Axis4` keeps the axis square to the A axis (about X).
  - Mandatory continuous facet checks cover the full cone and the supplied physical shank and holder. They cover each complete cut, entry and exit. The stored `shank_avoid` option cannot disable this guard.
  - An edge with no clear pose follows the Deburr's unreachable-edge policy: skip with a note, or refuse by name.
  - The tool enters and leaves along a checked, bounded axis line. The entire cone stays above `bottom_z`. Pose changes, gaps and chamfer-plane corners split runs.
  - Each run declares a framed flat `EdgeBreak` cap (#1891).
- The exposed-edge scan moved from `finishing3d/deburr.rs` into the shared `finishing3d/deburr_scan.rs`. The 3D Deburr calls it in the same order.
- App wiring: kind row, seed, sanity door (lead minus lag inside the cap), generate arm, cache stamp, project DTO (`multi_axis_deburr`), heights, setup sheet, section mode, WCS refusals, sim break bound.
- MCP: `add_operation`, `edit_operation` and `set_operation_geometry` work with the new kind through the generic tools.
- UI: `multiaxis_deburr_page.rs` (Geometry: size, filters, unreachable policy; Passes: axis mode, lean, max tilt, shank avoid; Heights; Feeds). The kind has its own original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-multiaxis-deburr.svg`, PNG from `cargo xtask icons`).

## Cause

New feature (#1894). A vertical cone cannot break steep or vertical edges, so the 3D Deburr skips them.

## UI screenshots

The before images show revision `971c23faa026865be47e425a660439f8c3d17ecd`, an ancestor of this PR's base. The new kind is absent there.
The after images show the original feature head `c2560be2bc4f8900f5cc238bb5879742ff8169d5`. The safety fixes below do not change the UI.
These are actual application window captures. They show the operation controls and entry. They do not show generated toolpaths.
The images are stored only on the fork's images-only `pr-screenshots` branch, commit `849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775`.

The new Passes page shows the axis mode, lead, lag, tilt cap and shank avoidance controls.

![After: Multi-Axis Deburr Passes page at c2560be2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/849e3eeba9e01f8f2ce72691074d81ab12b27775/pr-3283/after-passes-c2560be2.png)

## Safety review fixes on the new head

Final head: `a312b20ebdb48c2505ec417c6008d5cc1c6569d4`.

- Each candidate trims the edge until the tip and the lowest cone-rim point stay at or above `bottom_z` on every pass.
- Continuous outer convex polyhedra enclose the cone and the physical tool bands along the entire cutting segment.
- Facet clipping permits cone and cutting-flute contact only within the finite requested chamfer prism. Floors, other faces and material past an edge end receive no exemption.
- The same continuous checks cover the complete entry and exit lines. Clearance endpoints must put the whole tool above the part. The first plunge stages the axis change above every part face plus the largest tool radius and 1 mm.
- An axis that is too flat or requires more than 100 tool diameters of reach is refused. Unsafe segments use the existing named skip or refuse policy.
- The app supplies the physical shank and holder even when `shank_avoid` is false. The kernel guards the operation because column stock simulation does not judge posed cuts.

Regression pins:

- `the_brick_keeps_the_tilted_tip_and_entire_cone_above_the_bottom`: complete cone and tip stay above the brick's programmed bottom; clear vertical edges still cut.
- `a_raised_bottom_clips_the_cone_without_a_part_floor_to_hide_the_error`: a raised window isolates the bottom guard from the part floor.
- `a_boss_on_a_floor_skips_the_unsafe_foot_and_still_cuts_the_clear_edge`: the window extends below the floor; the unsafe foot is skipped and the clear upper edge still cuts.
- `an_obstacle_on_the_entry_line_is_skipped_while_clear_edges_still_cut`: an obstacle away from the cut blocks the entry or exit; other edges still cut.
- `an_unsafe_entry_refuses_by_name_when_skipping_is_disabled`: the picked edge cuts without the obstacle and refuses with the obstacle.
- `disabling_shank_avoid_cannot_bypass_the_mandatory_holder_collision_guard`: the option is off; an obstacle that misses the cone and shank still blocks the holder.

Mutation checks (each restored byte for byte):

- Ignored the pose offset in bottom clipping: the raised-window pin failed with a cone below `bottom_z`. Restored: passed.
- Disabled cone facet checks: the boss-floor pin failed with a cone in the floor. Restored: passed.
- Checked only the cut and omitted the entry/exit sweeps: the entry-obstacle pin failed when the tip crossed the obstacle. Restored: passed.
- Omitted the physical shank and holder from the app adapter: the option-off holder pin failed. Restored: passed.
- Sent the first plunge directly to the tip: the existing MCP generation pin failed with two mid-turn shank findings. Restored: passed.

Validation:

- Full quick gate on predecessor `93e571af99028af87a1dbdcf00cae796d57fa628`: 515 of 516 steps passed in 36.5 minutes. Only `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size` failed at its existing stale golden. The Slot test and golden are unchanged by this fix.
- The final commit removes one redundant `let` binding. It does not change the guarded geometry or the tests.
- Final-head quick selection: `motion suites: lib` and `app suites: mcp_multiaxis_deburr` passed both steps in 1.9 minutes. Motion: 530 passed, 10 ignored. MCP: 4 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed on the exact final source tree.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed all 242 steps on the final head in 40.9 minutes. The reached lanes were `motion heavy` and `app heavy`. All 102 ordinary ignored tests passed. All six registered known-fail checks matched their expected failures.
- All 13 `multiaxis::deburr_axis_tests` passed in release mode on the final head. This includes all five new kernel safety pins.

The recorded gate runs used `CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`. An earlier run with incompatible build artifacts was excluded. No golden, screenshot, log or review image is part of these fix commits.

title: feat(chamfer): select a tip offset
body:
## What changed

- Add a 2D Chamfer `Tip offset` setting.
- Offset closed loops and selected open chains toward physical air.
- Lower the virtual tool tip by `(tip offset + chamfer width) * tan(angle)`.
- Keep the active cone band between the tip offset and the chamfer outer radius.
- Refuse offsets that fold, disappear, use the wrong Side, cross material, exceed the tool radius, or exceed flute reach.
- Keep the `EdgeBreak` on the original selected edge with the authored width and depth.
- Add UI help, project version 74 migration, project round-trip support, and MCP create/edit/read support.
- Keep zero offset as the exact legacy closed-loop and open-chain path.
- Keep `minimum_cone_radius` as the project and MCP field name for file compatibility.

Stacked on #3059. This branch starts at the #3059 head and must follow that PR.

## How tested

- Focused motion tests: the final cone band, closed-loop Side, open-chain air side, zero compatibility, and offset refusals pass.
- Focused app tests: tool radius, flute reach, project JSON, project migration, and default compatibility pass.
- Focused MCP test: create, patch, read, save, and reset to zero pass.
- Focused UI tests pass:
  - `chamfer_geometry_exposes_tip_offset`

title: feat(wire): export a selected Agie opening for zero-step inspection
body:
The DXF import and Wire Contour selection prerequisites merged in #3193 and #3205. This PR adds the native zero-step inspection export.

The maintainer confirmed that the dependency and Agie-CAM reference approvals from #2951 also apply here. This PR gets its own safety review and trial-merge test after #2951 merges. [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3219#issuecomment-7080044891)

## Change

Use `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project> <operation> <new-directory>` for a saved operation.

A user can create an unassigned wire inspection operation on the Post page and choose one placed, closed DXF chain and an internal start. The user can save the operation and export a native Classic Cut 2S ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. The CLI and MCP use the same entry points.

The exporter preserves the nominal line and circular arc geometry. It checks the source selection, closure, winding, rounding, arc extrema, start disk and supported mounted machine axes. It refuses a changed or unsuitable selection and a destination that exists. An inspection work does not become a qualified machining operation.

This first setup uses 10 mm height, a 3 mm internal start and a 0.25 mm wire. The reference piece has unknown physical X/Y dimensions. Its controller fields store zero length and breadth. The receipt identifies the unverified fixture, erosion settings, physical Z and perpendicular controller lead. It describes the controller’s quality request separately from an assigned erosion process. The nominal setup does not promise a historical start seam, lead or cut sequence.

## Verification on the refreshed head

Commit `d982d452b` merges upstream main at `4e0c81964` into the contributor branch. The only manual resolution was the generated MCP reference. The compiled registry and the published reference list the same 119 tools. A trial merge with main at `6308a5db5` completed without conflicts.

The targeted author check passed 104 tests on this head. These covered post (6), MCP (3), desktop (3), application regressions (74) and geometry (18). Strict all-target Clippy passed for the four touched crates. The complete quick selector listed 1,048 steps. The author ran the targeted quick alternative.

The refreshed CLI imported an unchanged drawing, reopened the saved operations and exported two native jobs. All six files matched the controller-checked files byte for byte. Each receipt reported zero working steps. Repeat exports refused to overwrite either job.

The official heavy gate passed all 254 selected steps in 62.7 minutes on this revision. The command exited with status 0.

```sh
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 4e0c81964
```

## Earlier verification on `d13c5eed1`

Contributor head: `d13c5eed15251af0a903396c1d96bba298b644d0`. Parent: `2d0fa64841a1b42dbacb330f75f6bab61897da10`.

All eight scoped tests passed on this earlier head: two post tests, three MCP tests and three desktop tests. Strict all-target Clippy passed for geometry, post, app and UI. The independent synthetic export preserved every directed edge, arc center and resource link. It wrote one start, one work and zero steps. The checks include:

- `agie_inspection_accepts_listed_chain_and_checks_mounted_travel_in_the_wcs`
- `saved_selected_opening_exports_zero_steps_through_the_desktop_action`
- `unassigned_inspection_opening_survives_undo_redo_and_project_reopen`
- `setup_post_inspection_fields_and_submit_fit_the_visible_panel`

On this earlier revision, 252 of 253 heavy steps passed. The bulk release build failed to link two test binaries when the device ran out of space. The refreshed revision has its own gate run.

The desktop authoring and selection use a real undoable operation. The documented MCP reference was regenerated from the compiled CLI. The public selection returned by `list_features` can be passed directly to `create_agie_inspection`. A regression narrows the mount travel and reverses an axis. Each case refuses before file creation.

We used an offline VM running a copy of the actual Agie Classic Cut 2S control. The control opened native files produced by CAMCraft. We checked the program and ISO identities, nominal orientation, hole size and position, setup height, zero separation and zero working steps. Each work-level formal check blocked on undefined working technology. Each whole-piece check also flagged the low zero X/Y dimensions. Both control previews rendered the bound nominal profiles. An identical repeat import with the quality already present kept zero assigned working steps. Repeating an export to the same directory preserved the old files. No physical cut was made.

No model data, original job or simulator software is included. The public geometry tests are original synthetic cases. This inspection slice does not qualify a working erosion process, a physical slug restraint or an automatic cutting release. #3178 remains open for qualified curved die cutting. #3179 retains its physical process requirements.

## Desktop comparison

Both images use the same synthetic project and 750 by 830 pixel setup panel. The parent has the existing post controls. The new form shows the selected opening, wire and both start coordinates.

| Parent | This change |
| --- | --- |
| ![Parent setup Post panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-before.png) | ![Setup Post panel with the Agie inspection form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-after.png) |

Effort: high. No escalation.

Changelog: Export a selected closed DXF opening as a native, zero-step Classic Cut 2S inspection setup from desktop, CLI or MCP.

Refs #3178

title: feat(ui): load machine and post files from the user's disk in the browser
body:
## What changed

The browser build now loads the user's own machine (`.mch`) and post (`.cps`) files. The bytes come from the browser, not from a path.

- **Load machine (.mch)** and **Load post (.cps)** are live in the browser. They open the browser file picker. A picked machine is mounted. A picked post is selected.
- The Machine page has a new button **Load folder (.mch, .cps)** in the browser build only. It opens `<input webkitdirectory multiple>`. It adds each `.mch` and `.cps` file of the folder to the session lists. It does not need the File System Access API.
- A drop with a `.mch` or `.cps` file goes to a new module `setup_file_drop`. One file is mounted or selected. Several files only join the lists. One status line counts the files that landed and names each refused file with its reason.
- On the desktop, one dropped `.mch` or `.cps` on disk goes to `LoadMachineFile` or `SelectPostFile` by its full path.
- The domain module `camcraft_post::session_files`, re-exported by app, keeps each file by its bare name for the session, on the thread that loaded it. The caller passes app machine validation and holder-aware parsing as a callback. A file enters it only when it passes the checks of a file from disk: a machine must validate and parse, a post must compile and run.
- The readers of machine and post files consult the session store first, then the disk. So `LoadMachineFile`, `SelectPostFile` and the MCP tools run unchanged. Each mount and post choice stays one undo step.
- Session machines show in the machine catalogue (`library::enumerate`). Session posts show in the post combo list.
- A saved project that names a session file which is not loaded again is refused by that name (#2319). There is no fallback.

## Cause

The browser build had no disk and no picker for these files. `browser_files::refusal` greyed Load machine and Load post with `NEEDS_PICKER`. The file drop took model files only. The readers of `PostRef::File` and the machine file read only from disk.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/browser_setup_files.rs`:

- `a_dropped_mch_mounts_by_its_name_and_one_undo_takes_it_away`
- `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes`
- `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_malformed_pick_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`
- `a_picked_folder_fills_both_lists_and_a_picked_file_mounts_or_selects`
- `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` (AccessKit label, role `Button`, enabled state for "Load machine (.mch)", "Load folder (.mch, .cps)" and "Load post (.cps)"; no folder button on the desktop)

Other tests:

- `session_files::tests::a_bad_file_is_refused_by_name_and_never_kept` (post unit test). `an_unloaded_session_post_is_refused_by_name_at_post_time` pins a project that names a file that is not loaded.
- `setup_file_drop::tests::one_file_is_for_its_own_kind_in_any_case`.
- Updated for the new law: `browser_files::tests::every_picker_and_folder_command_is_refused_by_name_in_the_browser`, `a_picker_the_browser_lacks_is_refused_by_name_not_ignored`, `a_file_button_is_greyed_with_its_reason_in_the_browser`.

Red before the fix (reduced pins on unchanged `upstream/main`):

- the drop pins failed with `drop refused: drop-2950-vmc.mch is not a model file (read: .stl, .obj, .step, .stp, .sc, .solidcraft)`;
- the button pin failed with `LoadMachineDialog runs the browser's picker` / `left: Some("Not available in the browser yet: ...")`.

Mutation checks (old code put back, pins run, code restored):

- `crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs` from upstream: `the_machine_and_post_load_buttons_are_live_in_the_browser` red.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs` from upstream (drop route not called): the three drop pins red.
- `crates/app/src/posting.rs` from upstream (no session read at post time): `a_dropped_cps_is_selected_and_posts_from_its_bytes` red.
- `session_files::add_post` without its compile check: `several_dropped_files_land_and_each_bad_one_is_refused_by_name` red.
- All pins green again after each restore.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran all 428 steps on the previous head. 427 passed. `ui suites: lib` failed in three machines-pane tests. The cause was a process-global store: the session machines of the new tests leaked into the machine list of tests on other threads.
- The fix makes the store thread-local. The browser runs on one thread.
- On the final head, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only "app suites: lib" --only "ui suites: lib"` is green (ui lib 1385 passed, 0 failed). Only `crates/app/src/session_files.rs` changed between the two heads, plus one test comment and the decision file. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- The wasm32 build. The `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target is not installed on this machine, so the wasm-only code was not compiled. That code is: the folder input and batch read in `file_pick.rs`, the async drop read in `setup_file_drop.rs`, and the dialog openers in `state_picked.rs`. A reviewer with the target must run `cargo check -p camcraft-ui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- A real browser. The tests use `State::browser_build` and in-memory drops as the stand-in.
- Persistence in IndexedDB. Not built. The decision file lists the options for the maintainer.

## Overlaps

- #3057 changes `file_drop::take_drop`. This PR does not change that function. It adds `setup_file_drop::take`, which `shell.rs` calls before `take_drop`. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- Several open PRs touch `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and `crates/ui/src/state.rs` in other functions. This PR changes only `script_of`, `resolve_cps` (one line each), the `LoadMachineDialog` / `SelectPostDialog` arms and one new `CommandKind` variant.

## MCP

No new MCP tool. The browser routes go through the existing `LoadMachineFile` and `SelectPostFile` commands, and the MCP machine and post tools read the session store through the same readers. `LoadSetupFolderDialog` is a browser-only picker. It changes no document state.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/2950-browser-machine-post-files.md`.

Effort: high

Changelog: The browser build loads your own machine (.mch) and post (.cps) files from a picker, a folder picker or a drop; a bad file is refused by name.

Fixes #2950

## Review fixes

- A different post under an existing name is refused. Identical text is accepted. `same_name_folder_and_picker_leave_the_selected_post_and_history_stable` pins the selected post and history.
- One browser batch has a 32 MiB raw-byte limit. Both file lists share a 32 MiB retained-name-and-text limit. Refusals name the file. `individually_allowed_files_cannot_exceed_the_batch_budget` and `retained_text_budget_covers_both_lists_and_refuses_by_name` pin the limits.
- A successful machine import invalidates the machine catalogue. `a_folder_machine_import_invalidates_the_populated_catalogue` starts with a populated catalogue and pins the refreshed list.
- Pure storage and readers belong to `camcraft-post`. App supplies its existing machine checks through a callback. `pure_session_readers_are_available_without_the_app` pins the domain API.

## Machine and Post page images

These images show the shipped pages through the native render harness with the browser flag enabled. They are not browser captures.
Before uses the actual PR parent page and browser refusal code. After uses the review fix source.
The capture checks that the old load buttons are disabled, the new load buttons are enabled, and the folder button appears.

## Heavy lanes

Validated unchanged head `5e7c2b0d006c543316df6c062608aa2969c01722` on 2026-11-22.
The run used freshly fetched `upstream/main` at `148a5c832aa811bab9cae5c7f69e0ad945ee92d4`.

title: feat(ui): show the operator side at the work envelope
body:
## What changed

The viewport now shows the operator side of the work envelope. An arrow starts at the lower edge of the operator-side face. The arrow points out of the envelope, toward the operator. The text "Operator side" is at the tip of the arrow.

- `camcraft-post`: a machine file can state `general.operator_side`. The words are `"-X"`, `"+X"`, `"-Y"` and `"+Y"`. The word names the world axis that points from the envelope to the operator.
  - The field is optional. Old machine files and old projects load without a change.
  - A wrong word refuses the file by name. A wrong word never reads as the default.
  - `OperatorSide::default_for` gives the default of each machine kind: `+Y` for a lathe, `-Y` (the front) for each other kind.
- `camcraft-ui`: `operator_side.rs` builds the arrow when its input changes (the placed envelope and the side). Each other frame reads the kept arrow. The text is screen text, so it stays readable when the view turns.
- The View door has a new box, "Show operator side". It is view state: on by default, no command, not saved. It is disabled while the work envelope is off.
- The arrow and the text use the envelope colour. They are outside the envelope, so they do not cover the part or the toolpath.
- Docs: `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the machine file grammar) and `docs/decisions/2632-operator-side.md` (the defaults for each kind).

## Cause

This is new work that the maintainer asked for. The viewport did not show from which side the operator looks into the work envelope.

## Before and after screenshots

Both captures use the seeded shell at 1280 × 720 with the HAAS VF-2 machine file mounted and the work envelope shown. The camera looks from the front. "Before" is the same scene with the new box off. With the box off, the scene is the same as on `upstream/main`.

title: fix(motion): Circular climbs to clearance between its rings
body:
## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs`: before each ring after the first, the tool climbs straight up to clearance at the end of the last ring. Then the ring's ladder enters from clearance, as the first ring does. This applies to the flat mode and to the vault.
- The unit tests of `circular.rs` move to `circular_tests.rs` with no change. This keeps `circular.rs` at 361 lines (it was 411 before this PR).
- Two goldens gain the one new climb move.
- New pins in `crates/motion/tests/circular_ring_links.rs` and `crates/app/tests/circular_ring_links.rs`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2898-circular-ring-links.md`.

## Cause

Each ring runs its own level ladder (ring-major order). The first descent of a ladder expects the tool at clearance. After the first ring, the tool stood on that ring's floor. The descent then made one diagonal rapid from the floor up to clearance over the next ring's start. That rapid crossed the core that the next ring had still to cut. Verification convicted it and held the post. A 5 mm hole with a Ø6 tool has only one ring, so the catalog case did not show the fault. The vault had the same diagonal rapid.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_link_between_circular_rings_clears_the_stock` (motion): plunge, helix and ramp entry; planar and default links; flat and vault. No lateral rapid under the stock top. The verifier convicts no rapid.
- `the_issue_case_climbs_to_clearance_between_its_rings` (motion): the issue's four rings (R 7, 5, 3, 1). Each traverse onto R 5, 3 and 1 is at clearance.
- `a_spliced_diagonal_link_between_rings_is_still_convicted` (motion): the real path is clean. A diagonal link of the old shape, spliced in, gets `RapidInStock`. This is the "post stays blocked for a deliberately unsafe link" part of Done.
- `a_multi_ring_circular_links_its_rings_over_the_stock_and_posts` (app): the issue's job through generate, verify and post. No warning, and the program posts, for the plunge and the ramp entry.

Red before the fix: yes. On unchanged code the app pin reports `RapidInStock { at: 69 }` and `RapidInStock { at: 119 }`, the moves that the issue names. The motion pin reports rapids under the stock top at moves 69, 119 and 169.

Mutation: the fix with the climb disabled makes all three motion pins red (the flat case and the vault case at moves 20 and 40). The fix restored makes them green.

Gate:

Verification head: `050d1a7051475c6634e7493b6c8aa7077a959eeb`.
Invocation base: `upstream/main` at `1d5de9aeb846b83ee69a6cbbfd6f2ee8cdd3230e`.
The effective diff merge base was `0b8f4879dd88afe5f658a18c5dde035a88be41e3`.
These runs tested the unchanged final head directly.

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: green. All 240 steps passed in 45.3 minutes.
- Every reached motion heavy target ran. Its 37 steps had 59 ordinary test passes and two accepted expected-failure controls for #1950.
- Every reached app heavy target ran. Its 202 steps had 44 ordinary test passes and two accepted expected-failure controls for #1950 and #2849.
- One shared release build completes the 240 heavy steps. No unexpected failure occurred.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. All 705 steps passed in 42.1 minutes.
- Motion `circular_ring_links`: all four tests passed, including `a_multi_ring_helix_keeps_both_the_clearance_lift_and_descent_tracking`.
- App `circular_ring_links`: its generation, verification, and posting test passed.
- `default_machine_missing`: all nine tests passed, including `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`.
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green in 33 seconds.
- Heavy used a job budget of 24. Quick used eight jobs and `CAMCRAFT_GATE_SWEEP=off` while heavy ran concurrently.
- Clippy ran with quick after heavy finished. No tracked file changed during verification.
- Another session advanced the local main reference after both gate plans started. The invocation base above applies to both runs.
- The latest finding required verification evidence. No source edit, new pin, or new mutation check was needed.

## Goldens moved

Two goldens. Each gains one line, `Rapid <x> <y> <clearance>`, at the first ring's end, with the same X and Y. The header move count goes up by one. No other line changes.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/circular_ring_arcs.cl`: 401 to 402 moves.
- `crates/app/tests/golden/circular_ramp_stay_down.cl`: 133 to 134 moves.

## Not exercised

- The helix entry with several rings is still refused. Each ring's helix touches the last ring's helix at the start of the ring, in the same depth band. The crossing law convicts that touch. The program is refused, not unsafe. Follow-up: #3109.
- I tried the pocket's z-major order for the flat mode on this branch. It removed the helix crossings, but the inner rings then started with an axial plunge that was not named, also under a ramp entry. Four ramp-entry tests went red. I dropped it (see the decision record).
- Pixel snapshots were not run.
- This verification used the configured sccache wrapper at `/home/mikekinney/.local/bin/sccache`.

## Overlaps

- #2842 changes `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs` too, in the level ladder calls (`cut_levels_under`, `levels_from`). This PR changes the lines before `run_level_walks` and moves the test module. Touches the same file, different lines; whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Circular with several rings no longer links its rings with a rapid through the stock; each ring after the first climbs to clearance first, so verification passes and the program posts.

Effort: high

title: Publish SHA256SUMS.txt with every release
body:
## What

The release workflow's `publish` job now writes a `SHA256SUMS.txt` covering every release asset and uploads it with the other files.

- A new step runs `sha256sum` in `dist/` over the same file patterns the job already publishes (zip, setup.exe, tar.gz, deb, rpm, dmg, AppImage, snap, flatpak, pkg.tar.zst), checks the result with `sha256sum -c`, and prints it to the log.
- `dist/SHA256SUMS.txt` is added to the `softprops/action-gh-release` file list.

The file uses standard `sha256sum` format (`<hash>  <filename>`), so users can verify a download with:

```
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt
```

## Why

I've asked for CamCraft to be added to ArtCraft Launcher as a community app (storytold/craft-launcher#1545). The launcher checks every download, including downloads of community apps, against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so CamCraft can't be listed until its releases include one. Checksums also help anyone who downloads the files by hand.

Releases that are already published don't change. The file will appear starting with the next tag.

## Testing

- The YAML parses.
- I ran the step's script on sample files: it lists each asset once, `sha256sum -c` passes, and `release-body.md` isn't included.
- I haven't run it in a real release. That will happen on the next tag.

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.

## Gates

All gates ran on the final head 4bd091166. This head merges `upstream/main` at 2d98d87be and adds the `strategy` field to main's new Bore literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 724 steps, 0 failed (113.0 min). It includes `motion suites: bore_helix`, `motion suites: equal_steps` and `app suites: bore_helical`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 240 steps (202 app heavy, 37 motion heavy, 1 build), 0 failed (63.8 min). The 6 known-fail steps (#1950, #2849) are red as expected.
- The earlier head c70e84309 had a quick gate of 687 steps and a heavy run of 231 steps, all green.

## Screenshots

The Bore operation page, rendered by the UI test harness (`egui_kittest`) from a real Bore operation.

| | Rings | Helical |
|---|---|---|
| Passes tab | ![Passes, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-rings.png) | ![Passes, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-helical.png) |
| Heights tab | ![Heights, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-rings.png) | ![Heights, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-helical.png) |

- Passes tab: the Strategy combo shows the two strategies. The Spring pass check shows only for Helical.
- Heights tab: the last Levels row is "Stepdown" for Rings and "Helix pitch" for Helical.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A non-centre-cutting tool helixes like any other tool. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

- A new SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads an SVG file into the same `dxf::Document` as the DXF reader. The sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, the `Sketch` entity and the project file are shared and do not change.
  - Elements: `path` (M L H V C S Q T A Z, absolute and relative), `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`, `rect` (with rx/ry), `circle`, `ellipse`.
  - Groups: `g` with `transform` (matrix, translate, scale, rotate, skewX, skewY). A `use` of an element in the same file is drawn.
  - Curves: an arc or circle that maps to a circle stays an analytic arc. Beziers and true ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm.
  - Units: `width` and `height` in mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px (96 px to the inch), with the `viewBox` and `preserveAspectRatio`.
  - Y is flipped about the page height, so the drawing looks as it does in the editor.
  - A top-level `g` is a layer (`inkscape:label`, else `id`).
  - Text, images, nested `svg`, `style`, clip paths, masks, hidden content and `use` of other files are skipped and counted by kind.
- A new undoable command, `ImportSvg` (`commands/import_svg.rs`). It wraps `ImportDxf`, so apply and invert are the same code.
- A new MCP tool, `import_svg` (`mcp/svg_tools.rs`), and a new script verb, `cam.importSvg`. They take the options of `import_dxf`.
- The user guide (units and coordinates) and the MCP tool table list SVG.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals (by name, never a panic)

- A file that states no physical size, until the caller gives the unit of one drawing unit. The size is never guessed. A unitless `width` counts as no physical size.
- A caller unit for a file that states its size (two sizes would disagree).
- Malformed XML, malformed path data, an unknown transform or a singular one.
- A zero or negative document size or viewBox. A negative shape size.
- A degenerate arc (a zero radius).
- Percent or font-relative lengths in shapes.
- A file over the import budget (bytes, elements, segments), nesting deeper than 256, and `use` chains deeper than 16 (a reference loop).
- A compressed `.svgz` file, and a file that is not UTF-8.

## Tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/svg.rs` (9 tests): a rectangle with a hole in mm (nesting, Y flip), in and pt and px and cm documents, no physical size, absolute and relative path forms, Beziers and arcs, nested group transforms and a sheared ellipse, a rounded rect with polyline and skipped content, merged short segments, compact path syntax.
- `crates/geometry/tests/svg_refusals.rs` (5 tests): malformed documents and paths, zero or negative sizes, the import budget, and a deterministic smoke fuzz (truncations and 1000 byte mutations).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_svg.rs` (2 tests): `import_svg` end to end (units, layers, chains, skipped notes, bounds, move, undo and redo, a 2D Contour on the profile, save and reopen, the script verb), and the command's refusals and undo step.
- Red before the fix: the pins did not compile on unchanged code (`unresolved import camcraft_geometry::svg`).
- Mutation checks. Each guard was removed, the pin went red, and then the guard was restored:
  - Y flip: red (4 tests).
  - Arcs stay analytic: red (4 tests).
  - Caller unit on a sized file is refused: red.
  - A unitless size is no physical size: red.
  - Zero-radius arc refusal: red.
  - `use` depth guard: red (stack overflow).
  - Short-segment merge: red.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0).
- Touched suites, all green:
  - geometry: `svg` 9, `svg_refusals` 5, `dxf`, `dxf_refusals`, `sketch_data`, `sketch_chains`, and the lib tests.
  - app: `mcp_svg` 2, `mcp_dxf` 2, `sketch_profile` 8, `sketch_project` 14, `scripting` 20 (it checks `cam.d.ts`), `mcp` 23, and the lib tests (290).
- The gate did not complete. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` falls back to the batch tier, because the diff touches `crates/geometry/src/lib.rs`. On this machine the shared sccache server stopped responding: each compile through it hung, including the jobs of other sessions. The gate sets the sccache wrapper itself, so it hung at the `post` build twice. Clippy and the suites above ran with the wrapper unset. The batch tier still needs a run: the post-merge gate, or a reviewer's `pr-test.yml` run.

## Goldens moved

None.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for a 2D Contour on an SVG profile. On `main`, a 2D Contour on a profile is accepted but does not generate yet: that is #1864 (PR #2716). Follow-up: #3042.
- The row for `import_svg` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The edit was blocked as a sensitive file in this session. A maintainer session can add it. Then that PR needs `Process change: yes`.
- No UI change: the app has no DXF profile import dialog yet, so there is no file dialog to extend.
- Nested `<svg>` viewports, CSS stylesheets, text to outlines and embedded images are out of scope (the issue says so). They are counted as skipped.

## Overlaps

- #2773 (draft, needs-rework) changes the stock check in `ImportDxf::build`. This PR does not change `build`. `ImportSvg` has its own copy of that 10-line check, so it does not get the #2773 change. If #2773 merges first, `ImportSvg` must get the same change.
- #2924 adds rows to `commands/mod.rs` and `script/mod.rs`, and changes `mcp/sketch_tools.rs`. This PR adds other rows to the two `mod.rs` files and puts its MCP tool in a new file. The files are the same and the functions are different. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2678 adds lines to `commands/mod.rs`. The lines are different.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

Effort: high

Fixes #1880

title: feat(waterjet): Waterjet Profile operation on a shared 2D sheet kernel
body:
## What changed

- **Shared 2D sheet kernel (`crates/motion/src/sheet/`).** The kernel code moves out of `plasma` and `wire_edm` without a change of behaviour:
  - `nest` (contour roles, inner-first cut order) and `ring` (kerf ring, walks), from `plasma`;
  - `laws` (kerf law, cover law) and `lead` (straight and arc leads), from `plasma`;
  - `arclen` (a ring by arc length), from `wire_edm::tabs`;
  - `open` (the one-sided offset of an open run), from `wire_edm::open`.

  A `Voice` keeps each refusal text word for word. Plasma and wire EDM now call the shared code.
- **Cover law.** The law now takes one span or more for each contour, and an `exempt` closure for a tab's bridge. Plasma exempts no point. The law now refuses a closed contour that has no span.
- **Waterjet generator (`crates/motion/src/waterjet/`).** `waterjet_profile` does these steps:
  - It cuts the inner contours first, with the kerf ring at kerf / 2 on the waste side.
  - It adds straight or arc leads, with the pierce in the scrap. A lead with no room is halved up to four times.
  - It pierces a tight hole at its centre when the lead has no room after the halving.
  - It cuts tabs as uncut gaps. Each stretch between two gaps gets its own pierce, lead-in and lead-out.
  - It cuts open runs on the centre line, or to the left or right of travel.
  - It can post G41/G42, and it can send arcs as chords (`Move::chords`).

  The kerf law and the cover law certify the result.
- **App.** The changes are:
  - `OpType::WaterjetProfile` (stored id 44), `Section::Waterjet` and `Family::Waterjet`. The op mounts a `ToolKind::Waterjet` nozzle only.
  - `WaterjetOp` with its command-door sanity check, `waterjet_op.rs` (seed, params, generate) and the digest bytes.
  - A `.camproj` DTO (`waterjet_profile`, additive).
  - Each exhaustive match in the app gets a waterjet arm.
  - Profile (DXF) sources are admitted. The family door has its own words: "mount a waterjet first".
  - MCP reaches the kind through the generic `add_operation` / `edit_operation`. The `add_operation` text now names waterjet.
- **UI.** The changes are:
  - `waterjet_page.rs` with these fields: kerf, compensation, direction, open-run side, send arcs as lines, sheet heights, tabs, lead shape and lengths, cut feed, pierce time, abrasive delay. It has no torch height or THC field.
  - The Waterjet ribbon section.
  - An original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-waterjet-profile.svg`, rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`).

## Readings

- Golden `waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes.cl` has 149 moves, 5 pierces and 3 holes cut before the outline. The outline is cut as two led-in stretches between 2 mm tabs.
- The existing goldens do not change. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` shows only the new file. The plasma golden `plasma_plate_with_holes.cl` stays byte-identical after the kernel move.

## Tests (pins)

Each pin was red before this change: the module and the kind did not exist, so the pins could not compile.

- motion `waterjet::tests` (9): `holes_are_cut_before_the_outline_and_every_pierce_is_in_the_waste`, `straight_leads_lay_no_arc_on_a_square_part`, `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_and_each_stretch_is_pierced_and_led_in`, `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre`, `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords`, `an_open_run_rides_its_stated_side`, `control_compensation_records_a_comp_span_per_untabbed_contour`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`, `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged`.
- app `waterjet_profile` (6): the family door, hole first, tabs, a milling tool refused, create / edit / undo / redo, and a byte-identical `.camproj` round trip.
- app `mcp_waterjet` (1): add, edit, undo, redo and generate over MCP.
- app `golden_cl::waterjet_tabbed_plate_with_holes_matches_golden`.
- ui `waterjet_ribbon_tests` (2): the section shows on a waterjet only, the tip names the waterjet, the glyph is its own, and the page has a leads tab.
- Plasma and wire EDM: all `camcraft-motion` plasma, sheet and wire tests pass, and all 34 `golden_cl` tests pass.

## Mutation results

Each mutation was applied, the pins were run, and then the code was restored (green again).

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Inner-first order removed | red: `holes_are_cut_before_...`, `a_tight_hole_...` |
| Tabs ignored | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...`, `bad_input_...` |
| Tight-hole rule off | red: `a_tight_hole_is_pierced_at_its_centre` |
| Linearization ignored | red: `linearize_sends_every_arc_as_chords` |
| Cover law exempts every point | red: `a_slot_narrower_than_the_kerf_is_refused_not_bridged` |
| Cover law exempts no point | red: `tabs_leave_uncut_gaps_...` (6 mm tabs) |
| Leads on the part side | red: 7 of 9 pins |

## Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 422 steps ran (374 app, 44 post, 3 motion, 1 cl). The only red steps were kind-count pins that this change extends on purpose: `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name`, `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` and `tests/ribbon.rs` (`family_is_derived_not_forked`, `the_probe_appends_its_id_and_lists_in_drilling`). I updated them to 45 kinds and the Waterjet section. Because I edited during the run, the gate marked that run VOID. `--failed` on the committed tree then ran the red step: green. The app lib suite is green (290).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 1324 passed, 0 failed. The waterjet row was added to `tips_match_the_imgui_table`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

- Review fix on `aded58c47` (merged with `upstream/main` `f036dddad`):
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 694 steps, 1 failed. The red step is `app suites: tool_gate` (`the_refusal_names_a_fitting_catalog_entry`). Its red row is `OpType::Finish3D`: `upstream/main` (#3069) adds `Router ball nose 6 mm` before `BN-0600` in the catalog, and the tie goes to the first entry. The step is red on `upstream/main` too. The waterjet row in the same test passes.
  - `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 237 steps, 0 failed. The lanes are `motion heavy` (37 steps), `app heavy` (199 steps) and the heavy build.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green.

## Not exercised

- Posting. No post serves `Kind::Waterjet` yet. The pierce time and the abrasive delay are in the path notes only. #1882 adds the CL record and the post hooks.
- `verify` and the post gate for a waterjet op. That is #1885.
- Selection of the cut data from the nozzle's recipe. This is follow-up #3047.
- The MCP skill row. The skill file is a protected path in this session. This is follow-up #3048.
- The UI page was not opened in an interactive window. The screenshots below come from the off-screen egui_kittest and wgpu render of the real shell.

## Screenshots

The images are on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch (commit `4dad162f3`, folder `pr-3058/v2/`). They come from the off-screen egui_kittest and wgpu render of the real shell on the same machine. The render code is not committed.

Before and after: the same waterjet machine ("Waterjet test") is mounted in both views.

| View | Image |
|---|---|
| Before (`upstream/main` `f036dddad`): ribbon, no Waterjet section | ![ribbon before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/4dad162f3261957ce4269e4f0b2fef4d99ee3aa3/pr-3058/v2/ribbon-before.png) |
| After (this PR): ribbon with the Waterjet section | ![ribbon after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/4dad162f3261957ce4269e4f0b2fef4d99ee3aa3/pr-3058/v2/ribbon-after.png) |

After (this PR): the op page at a width of 900 px. Each control is fully visible.

title: feat(post): waterjet records, CR LF, travel, programBounds and a generic waterjet post
body:
## Review fixes and final-head validation

Final head: `ca7ba50664f6d4605b96f468b17eccc6a04f5821`.

This update fixes the two findings in the latest review.

1. The engine preserves the original motion record's signed Z change on every generated chord. The waterjet post refuses that change before it writes a cutting block. Pin: `waterjet_post_refuses_a_helical_arc_in_both_arc_modes`. The test checks the named Z refusal and no cutting blocks in circular and linear modes.
2. The missing-machine test checks the CLI refusal separately from the generation log. Pin: `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation`. The test enables INFO logs and checks that the log names `Face1`. The selected refusal names `Setup2` and does not name `Face1`. The complete output still must name `Face2`.

Both pins pass. Each fix was removed separately. Each pin then failed with exit 101. Each restored fix passed.

Final-head results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. All 997 steps pass in 40.1 minutes.
- Clippy: GREEN in 78 seconds. All eight project crates pass with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: RED. All 234 steps ran in 33.8 minutes. One step failed.
- The failed step is `app heavy: pocket3d_hsm`. Its failed test is `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` at `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs:144`.
- The test produced `(3158, 3130, 1141)`. Its Linux assertion expects `(4726, 4698, 549)`.
- All other reached motion and app heavy steps pass. The gate accepted the declared known-fail checks.
- The same test fails on the exact parent source, `b8e5e7ef21b9595a41614db04ddabf27efd5f68f`, with exit 101 and the same counts. The check restored all five changed files byte-for-byte. This update makes no unrelated change.

The PR remains a draft. No screenshots, logs, or review evidence are committed.

The sections below describe the original implementation and its historical validation. Their test counts and gate results are historical.

## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 996 steps, 0 failed (wall 30.5 min; the `cl` change reaches each dependent crate). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branch history: the first commit was squashed onto a newer main by mistake, so it reverted nine files of the Tormach lathe G76 work (#2952). The second commit restores them from main. The net diff against main has only the #1882 files (34 files). The four new Tormach lathe test binaries pass on the combined tree. The quick gate ran on the base `768fe23f0`, before that main change; main's change since then touches none of the files of this PR.

## Goldens moved

None. All goldens are new: `crates/post/tests/golden/waterjet/plate.nc`, `plate_inch_chords.nc` and the input `plate.cnc`, plus `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/waterjet-iso/*.refusal`. No existing `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed.

## Not exercised

- No generator writes the waterjet records yet. The `Toolpath::waterjet` field and its `.cl` dump come with the WaterjetProfile operation (#1883). The input stream here is written by hand.
- The post is not in `posting::BUILTINS`, so the app does not offer it yet (see the decision record). A user can post with it as a file of their own (`serves = ["waterjet"]`).
- The post did not run on a real waterjet control.

## Overlaps

- #3037 changes `engine.rs` (the `Script::load` line in `run_program_with`) and `js.rs`. This PR touches the same file, different lines. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2893 changes `engine.rs` and `js.rs` (fine boring). Same file, different function. Whichever merges second refreshes.

Changelog: Post: generic ISO abrasive-waterjet post (`waterjet-iso.cps`), WATERJET / JET stream records with `onJetOn` / `onJetOff`, CR LF output (`lineEnding`), `machine.travel`, `programBounds` and arc linearization (`linearizeArcs`) for scripts.

Effort: high

Fixes #1882

title: fix(post): leave Agie jobs unarmed until the loaded work quality is verified
body:
Stacked on #2993. Review the [quality-binding correction above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/feb802a77a99878951d5faf5ba2f41f65270c018...814dca499f9f9793f3c9e6bcd3eafab5f32e2022).

## Author gate status

The guarded source at cfc281268 passed the complete reached heavy gate, 247/247 steps in 58.1 minutes on macOS arm64. It includes the separate default-machine correction merged upstream in #3092. The mixed-condition regression passed in the 19-test Agie writer module. Both input orders received the exact error and no files.

On the corrected production source 766fc7109, the regular CLI exported all 20 synthetic jobs. Their 32 works and 72 native files matched the previous guarded outputs byte for byte. All 20 controller-review receipts matched. All 20 repeat attempts refused to replace an existing job and preserved every byte. This corpus is a software comparison. The real control checks below cover the stated representative jobs.

The full quick gate on 766fc7109 found the missing dedicated test suite for the built-in Agie CPS dispatcher. The next commit added the suite and its 11 expected refusal records. Passing each record requires the direct single-file post to fail with the native-job diagnostic and leave no NC file.

The final head is 814dca499. It changes only tests above cfc281268. On a real plasma stream and 1300PL machine, the Agie single-file dispatcher must fail with its specific native-directory diagnostic. The workspace must exclude the post from the plasma registry. The single-file smoothing test now uses the workspace's native-post predicate. With smoothing enabled, a mounted Agie punch must refuse the setup and create no job directory. The other posts retain their previous checks.

All 49 targeted tests passed on the final head: seven plasma, seven smoothing, 12 native app, 11 native dispatcher and 12 recorded-stream tests.

The original full quick on cfc281268 ran 1,013 steps in 80.6 minutes. All but the two cross-post tests passed, including strict Clippy. On 814dca499 the official failed-step replay selected both suites and passed both in 0.8 minutes. Each suite ran seven tests. The complete 247-step heavy result belongs to cfc281268. The whole quick and heavy gates have not been repeated on 814dca499.

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 211105042b817a5b32fdf2c971d42e6d968297c6 --failed gate-logs/quick-20261121-023002
```

```sh
cargo test -p camcraft-app --test plasma_post_refusals --test smoothing --test agie_native
cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_agie_native --test recorded_streams
```

## Integration order

The maintainer requests a separate P1 change from main and a safety-tier review of each feature PR. The standalone zero-step encoder is #3104. The first workspace writer in #2951 uses it. Keep earlier feature drafts that still generate erosion steps on hold until each takes its own safety correction and review. The standalone machine template in #2948 has no writer.

## Gate commands and pinning tests

The earlier macOS bore fixture and missing operation name were reproduced on ba5ff0ae1 with these commands:

```sh
cargo xtask gate quick --base 1d81b609c --only 'app suites: default_machine_missing'
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 1d81b609c --only 'app heavy: pocket3d_hsm'
```

The scoped CLI and native writer checks include:

- `native_punch_links_its_three_files_and_uses_the_uncompensated_contour`
- `every_punch_has_its_own_geometry_and_uses_the_requested_piece_quality`
- `nine_model_owners_resolve_all_resources_and_the_same_registered_quality`
- `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero`
- `the_saved_condition_selects_the_exact_requested_quality`

A stale native quality can change the effective Ra, pass count and wire offsets while the controller formal check passes. A 40 mm Cobra trial bound the same 0.30 request to different existing records. The wrong selection ran three passes at 0.245, 0.165 and 0.140 mm. The intended selection ran four at 0.250, 0.170, 0.145 and 0.135 mm. A deliberately conflicting semantic name also defeated the returned handle and success-status checks after a new piece import.

CAMCraft now writes a complete native setup bundle and leaves every work with zero erosion steps. Geometry, start holes, work definitions and separation settings are present. The bundle records a stable quality name for the requested tuple and checks each assignment. The operator must review each effective native work in place before generating any machining steps. The operator can correct a mismatched quality without importing the piece again.

Check the actual wire, stock height, Ra, Tkm, Te and visible options in Work Details. For a mismatch, use Quality (Kwaliteit) and Define (Definiëren) on that same work. Confirm the requested values. Open Technology (Technologie), select TECCUT, and use Assign (Toewijzen) on the matching row. Check the individual working steps and their offsets before running GRAFICHECK and FORMALCHECK. The user guide gives the full procedure and the expected values for each supported setting. The native dialog exposes two of the three authored checkbox values.

On the deliberately polluted installation, a new import showed both works at [0]. FORMALCHECK reported a blocking technology error for each. Correcting Ra on the first work kept both at [0]. Explicit TECCUT assignment armed only the checked work. The installation retained the other unarmed work until its own review. The saved two-work piece then passed FORMALCHECK. GRAFICHECK produced 16 correctly ordered profile and separation blocks. All nine nominal faces had the verified 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm offsets. Both rough bridges measured 1.000 mm. The two cutting envelopes remained disjoint. The effective Ra 0.30 Berco process was checked independently at 15, 20, 40 and 80 mm. No physical cut was made.

The independent gate passed 96 app tests, 18 native post tests and three geometry tests. The app count includes machine, machine library and posting suites. It exported 20 jobs with 32 works. All 52 geometry and resource files matched previous output. Each of the 20 piece files changed from automatic machining to setup-only. Each repeat export preserved every file. Strict Clippy passed for the app, post, UI and geometry libraries. The final source revision reproduced all 72 files and reported working_steps_generated=false for all 20 jobs. Later changes clarify the repeat-import result and pin the refusal for mixed wire conditions.

After manual release and plotting of both a mixed-radius Ra 0.30 piece and a rectangular Ra 0.35 piece, the tester reimported each exact SBL on its existing control. Each import created a new default-named piece with the intended ISO resource and zero steps. FORMALCHECK again reported technology undefined. The earlier named piece stayed separate. Select the newly created row and confirm its geometry and [0] before assigning the technology.

The real GUI status before the change reported the posted job. After the change it reports zero working steps, the requested targets, wire and stock values, and the required offsets. Both screenshots show the same synthetic cutoff job, DEMO2999, after the desktop Post command. The new receipt lists the control checks and the offsets of 245, 155, 140 and 134 µm.

**Before · `feb802a77`**

![Earlier Post receipt reporting three files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-before.png)

**After · `814dca499`**

![Current Post receipt reporting zero working steps and the required control checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/579ee692c2b26e6aca37776f5319067443c742a1/pr-2999/receipt-after.png)

Effort: high
Changelog: Agie native jobs import with zero machining steps. Review each work's effective native quality and offsets before assigning its technology in Agie Control.

Fixes #2984
